She notes that cutting-edge satellites are now orbiting the Earth at a greater cadence, providing increasingly high-resolution spatial imagery that can offer early warning signs of any deterioration in forest health. As the pace of climate change escalates, monitoring threats to tropical forests – and, ultimately, intervening to counter these threats – has never been so important. L-band SAR, a less advanced technology than P-band, has been key to helping scientists realise that Africa’s forests and woody savannahs have already passed a tipping point. According to findings published in the journal Scientific Reports , rapid deforestation means these African biomes have been releasing more carbon than they sequester since 2010. Logs lie next to a rusting barge on the banks of the Congo river. REUTERS/David Lewis Alongside continuous innovation in the hardware of satellites, breakthroughs on the software side are enabling scientists to make ever-greater use of satellite data. “We have now, through the use of AI capabilities, the ability to really interrogate these datasets on a massive scale,” says Lyndsay. This is paving the way for a significant expansion in predictive analytics, she says. A company might, for example, receive an alert that signals of impending deforestation have been detected within areas from which its sources commodities. Armed with this data, the company could then consider taking preventative action. The Congo rainforest stretches across Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Congo-Brazzaville, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon, as well as DR Congo itself. With much of its expanse virtually inaccessible by road, Satellites offer the only practical way of keeping track of deforestation threats. “I don't think there's any way that we could possibly have oversight of all natural forests globally, without having some sort of bird’s-eye view of what's going on,” says Lucy Barnes, a senior manager for supply chain solutions at the Earthworm Foundation. The non-profit has been running a satellite monitoring platform called Starling with Airbus since 2016 that can alert major companies to risks of deforestation in their supply chains. Improved technology will open new possibilities for using satellite data, Barnes adds. “It's not necessarily about using it just for monitoring deforestation, as such. I think in some ways, we’re able to do that to a very high level now. It's how you can also use that data for answering other environmental questions, for example, measuring carbon sequestration.” Indeed, multiple actors in the carbon markets space are already making extensive use of satellite data. The hope is that satellite data could even help solve some of the longstanding problems that have undermined the growth of these markets. REDD+ carbon credit schemes have been heavily promoted as a way to avoid emissions linked to deforestation, yet these schemes have repeatedly been criticised for alleged “over-crediting”. An image of Sumatra in western Indonesia via Starling, a satellite monitoring platform run by Earthworm Foundation and Airbus. Starling/Handout via REUTERS In a notorious example, project developer Carbon Green Investments and environmental consultancy South Pole grossly overstated the rate of deforestation in a “reference area” close to the forest they were seeking to preserve through the Kariba REDD+ project in Zimbabwe. This allowed the developer to claim its interventions within the project area made a greater impact in avoiding emissions than was truly the case. Following a lengthy investigation, carbon markets registry Verra found last year that the project had issued more than twice as many credits as it should have done. In the wake of these reputational disasters, the price of avoided deforestation credits remains depressed. Even higher-rated REDD+ credits trade at only around $7 per tonne, according to data from carbon markets intelligence firm Sylvera. By comparison, high-rated projects that remove carbon through reforestation or afforestation average $26.10 per tonne. Yet experts agree that there is no higher priority for climate and biodiversity than protecting existing forest habitats. In other words, there is a misalignment in the market between the financial value of afforestation versus the conservation value of avoiding deforestation in the first place. Satellite monitoring could help solve this conundrum. Phil Platts, senior vice president for geospatial and Earth observation at carbon ratings agency BeZero Carbon, notes that newer avoided deforestation methodologies – such as Verra’s VM0048 – take responsibility for determining the baseline used to calculate deforestation rates away from project developers. Instead, registries use satellite imagery to calculate deforestation rates across a country or province; credit issuance is then based on comparing deforestation in the project area with the wider jurisdiction. The “systematic over-crediting” that once marred avoided deforestation projects “just isn’t there with these new methodologies,” Platts says. Finland-based ICEYE is partnering with the Jane Goodall Foundation to support chimpanzee conservation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo by using SAR to detect logging and illegal mining. REUTERS/James Akena Despite these advances, the carbon markets remain controversial. Rainforest Foundation UK’s executive director Joe Eisen describes the market as a “folly” in the forests of central Africa, warning that revenues are “not filtering down to communities where it's most needed”. Nevertheless, Rainforest Foundation UK is working on a pilot project in 30 community forests in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in which communities receive payments based on protecting forest cover. The verification of results is “based entirely on satellite data”, Eisen says. The NGO also operates a satellite monitoring platform called ForestEye, which can provide community forest monitoring groups with access to intelligence on disturbance to the forest canopy. As both hardware and software continues to improve, satellite technology will play an increasingly key role both in monitoring forest carbon projects, and in supporting rainforest conservation more generally. One company pushing the boundaries of what satellite monitoring can do is ICEYE, a Finland-headquartered company that operates the world’s largest constellation of SAR satellites. In April, it announced a partnership with the Jane Goodall Foundation to support chimpanzee conservation in eastern DRC by using SAR to detect threats such as logging and illegal mining. Michael Bennett, ICEYE’s head of government solutions, says conventional satellite monitoring is insufficient in this region, which is blanketed by thick clouds for much of the year. Illegal activities can easily remain undetected beneath the thick forest canopy. DRC has been losing roughly 0.5% of its primary forests each year over the past decade, largely due to encroachment of small-scale agriculture. REUTERS/Arlette Bashizi “With SAR, you don't need to get lucky,” he says. Much like the ESA’s Biomass satellite, the radar beams transmitted by ICEYE’s satellites can penetrate both cloud and canopy cover to build a 3D image that make it easier to detect possible threats. And while conservation organisations might traditionally rely on satellite images that are several months, or even years, out of date, Bennett stresses that ICEYE’s constellation of dozens of satellites in low Earth orbit mean the company can provide “near-real time” coverage. Of course, gaining these kinds of insights is only the first step. There is still the problem of how to intervene in an environment where the government’s authority is limited at best. With a more accurate picture of threats to chimpanzees, however, Bennett suggests the Jane Goodall Foundation will be able to become more proactive in alerting authorities and on-the-ground team to the need for action. Sassan Saatchi is CEO of CTrees, a platform that offers free access to data on carbon sequestration down to the level of an individual tree. While hailing the advances in satellite technology, he says more work is needed to ensure that increasingly abundant sources of data are actually used by local teams, both in carbon projects and in broader conservation efforts. “There is so much free material and technology they can use,” he says. “If they use it, it would be a significant change.” The dangers facing the great forests of central Africa and their wealth of biodiversity remain formidable. DRC has been losing roughly 0.5% of its primary forests each year over the past decade, largely due to encroachment of small-scale agriculture. And Cameroon suffered its worst ever year of deforestation in 2025, partly driven by the growth of cocoa plantations. Thanks to satellite data, governments, NGOs and companies have a clearer picture than ever before on the health of Africa’s forests. The challenge now, with the help of satellite tools, is to find ways to ensure these green lungs can survive forever. This article is from the latest issue of The Ethical Corporation magazine, on deforestation risk. You can download the digital pdf of the magazine by clicking here

item.title: Neue Regierung Ungarns plant deutliche Senkung des Haushaltsdefizits
item.description: Ungarn strebt für das kommende Jahr eine deutliche Senkung seines Haushaltsdefizits auf 4,9 Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts (BIP) an. Den entsprechenden Haushaltsentwurf stellte Ministerpräsident Peter Magyar am Montag vor. Das Vorhaben gilt als wichtiger Prüfstein für die Glaubwürdigkeit des Ziels, den Euro einzuführen. Die geplante Verringerung wäre ein deutlicher Rückgang gegenüber dem für dieses Jahr erwarteten Defizit von 7,5 Prozent. Zudem ist das Ziel ehrgeiziger als die von Analysten in einer Reuters-Umfrage prognostizierten 5,3 Prozent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ungarn strebt für das kommende Jahr eine deutliche Senkung seines Haushaltsdefizits auf 4,9 Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts (BIP) an. Den entsprechenden Haushaltsentwurf stellte Ministerpräsident Peter Magyar am Montag vor. Das Vorhaben gilt als wichtiger Prüfstein für die Glaubwürdigkeit des Ziels, den Euro einzuführen. Die geplante Verringerung wäre ein deutlicher Rückgang gegenüber dem für dieses Jahr erwarteten Defizit von 7,5 Prozent. Zudem ist das Ziel ehrgeiziger als die von Analysten in einer Reuters-Umfrage prognostizierten 5,3 Prozent. Magyar versucht, das Defizit mittelfristig unter die EU-Obergrenze von drei Prozent - eines der Euro-Kriterien - zu drücken, ohne dabei seine Wahlversprechen zu brechen. Er hatte im April einen Erdrutschsieg über Viktor Orban errungen. Die geplanten Mehrausgaben sollen im kommenden Jahr mehr als zwei Billionen Forint (rund 5,7 Milliarden Euro) betragen. Gleichzeitig will die Regierung Einsparungen von 1,5 Billionen Forint (rund 3,8 Milliarden Euro) vornehmen. Die Einnahmen sollen durch eine neue Vermögenssteuer, eine höhere Körperschaftssteuer für Großkonzerne sowie höhere Steuern für Energieunternehmen gesteigert werden. Der Entwurf sieht zudem Steuersenkungen für mehr als zwei Millionen Steuerzahler im Umfang von 250 Milliarden Forint (rund 625 Millionen Euro) vor. Der Einkommensteuersatz auf den Mindestlohn soll auf neun Prozent sinken. Das Ziel der Euro-Einführung hatte zuletzt zu einer Aufwertung des ungarischen Forint beigetragen, was die Inflation unter das Inflationsziel der Zentralbank drückte. Die Renditen für Staatsanleihen fielen auf einen der niedrigsten Werte in Mitteleuropa. Am Montag legte der Forint gegenüber anderen Währungen der Region zu und erreichte den höchsten Stand seit vier Wochen. Analysten rechnen mit einem Beitritt Ungarns zur Eurozone in den Jahren 2032 oder 2033.

item.title: Energy Watch: Elections angst
item.description: Elections are always delicate moments. With Israel's parliamentary vote eight days away and the US midterms following a week later, oil markets are nervously watching the Middle East. Reported Iranian attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record 12 last week, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elections are always delicate moments. With [USN:FWN4630MG TEXT:"Israel's parliamentary vote"] eight days away and the [USN:L1N4600TJ TEXT:"US midterms"] following a week later, oil markets are nervously watching the Middle East. Reported [USN:S8N45501B TEXT:"Iranian attacks"] on ships around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record 12 last week, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency. What was most telling was not the number itself but the fact that UKMTO admitted that it is struggling to keep count of strikes, "with the majority of vessels attacked refusing to report." This surge in attacks appears to be having a significant impact on flows. Oil exports through the narrow waterway have fallen from a peak of 17 million barrels per day in early October to around 11 million bpd in recent days, Kpler data showed. Yet producers and shippers are still sailing through Hormuz, showing how quickly the industry has adapted to a new normal characterized by severely heightened risk. That resilience comes at a cost, however. Just ask Asian refiners. They purchase the majority of the Middle East's oil, and soaring shipping costs are crushing their profit margins. For more on that, [USN:L6N4620UK TEXT:"check out my latest column"]. Oil prices, meanwhile, hit a 5-month high of over $109 a barrel on Friday, reflecting growing angst among investors that the Iran war could reignite, with President Donald Trump saying the US might [USN:L6N4620Q7 TEXT:"renew strikes"] on Iran's nuclear facilities. Benchmark Brent oil prices slipped on Monday, however. In other news: China's economy [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"bounced back"] from a three-year low, growing 4.5% in the third quarter and beating forecasts as roaring exports offset consumers' tight grip on their wallets. The strong reading is another sign that the world's top oil importer has largely shielded itself from the worst effects of the Iran war. Chinese oil refineries raised processing rates slightly in September for a third straight month as strong fuel exports supported demand. The world's biggest oil buyer cut crude imports by 21.5% from a year earlier while boosting domestic production. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney is betting that a new pipeline can revive the country's oil industry, lift production and exports, and reduce the country’s dependence on the United States. Bringing back jobs will be much harder, writes Reuters correspondent Amanda Stephenson. The US and Israeli war against Iran has dominated the energy story in 2026. But the quiet retooling of power grids from Lagos to Manila may prove [USN:L1N45Z15T TEXT:"more significant"] in the long run, writes ROI Energy Transition Columnist Gavin Maguire. As ever, don't hesitate to contact me at ron.bousso@thomsonreuters.com or follow me on LinkedIn with any questions or thoughts. Subscribe to get Ron Bousso's Power Up newsletter delivered to your inbox every Monday and Thursday. Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: Menino de 13 anos é suspeito de esfaquear professora e aluno na Romênia após publicações no TikTok
item.description: A polícia romena informou que um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu uma professora e outro aluno na segunda-feira, em meio a relatos da mídia local de que ele havia postado sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A polícia romena informou que um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu uma professora e outro aluno na segunda-feira, em meio a relatos da mídia local de que ele havia postado sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque. As escolas na Europa têm enfrentado uma série de ataques este ano em países como Polônia, França e Suécia, com as autoridades, em alguns casos, apontando o papel das redes sociais e das subculturas online que glorificam o assassinato como fator que incita a violência. “Por volta das 8h40 (2h40 em Brasília), a polícia foi alertada... de que um aluno do sétimo ano de uma escola em Bistrita teria supostamente atacado uma professora e outro aluno com uma faca”, informou a polícia em comunicado. Uma fonte judicial disse à Reuters que o adolescente de 13 anos estava sendo investigado sob suspeita de tentativa de homicídio qualificado, mas, por ser menor de idade, não será julgado. A Reuters não conseguiu entrar em contato com o advogado do menino. A fonte disse que o menino havia postado mensagens no TikTok nas quais ele incitava à violência, mas afirmou que os promotores precisavam examinar seus dispositivos digitais antes de chegar a conclusões. Não houve comentário imediato do TikTok sobre o caso. Vários veículos de mídia locais noticiaram que o menino havia postado online sobre suas intenções pouco antes do ataque. Uma imagem de rede social publicada na mídia local mostrava um menino se fotografando no espelho do banheiro com uma faca e um capacete com uma câmera. Outra mostrava sua mão fazendo o sinal de “OK”. Abaixo, uma mensagem em inglês dizia: “É isso aí, rapazes. Venho preparando isso há 8 meses, vejo vocês no Valhalla”. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente a autenticidade das publicações. Seu conteúdo era semelhante ao postado por um agressor que matou um zelador de escola no leste da Polônia no início deste mês. “As notícias da imprensa de que o estudante anunciou seu ataque no TikTok devem ser esclarecidas pelos investigadores”, escreveu o ministro da Educação, Mihai Dimian, no Facebook.

item.title: Brasil registra foco de Doença de Newcastle em perus em Santa Catarina
item.description: O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, acrescentando que 133 granjas da região serão afetadas por medidas sanitárias.
item.dc:creator: Victor Borges
item.content:encoded: O Ministério da Agricultura registrou um foco de Doença de Newcastle em uma criação de perus em Santa Catarina, disse nesta segunda-feira o ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, acrescentando que 133 granjas da região serão afetadas por medidas sanitárias. Autoridades disseram ainda que o ministério está informando parceiros comerciais sobre o caso da doença viral altamente contagiosa para aves, que pode resultar em embargos comerciais às exportações do Brasil, o maior exportador global de carne de frango. A China, um dos principais destinos das exportações brasileiras de carne de frango, impôs em 2024 um embargo à carne de frango brasileira após a confirmação de um caso de Doença de Newcastle em uma granja comercial no Rio Grande do Sul. Outros países também chegaram a banir provisoriamente o produto brasileiro. Mas as autoridades acrescentaram que o ministério ainda não recebeu qualquer informação sobre suspensão das exportações brasileiras por conta do foco em perus, em um estabelecimento de avicultura comercial de corte no município de Nova Itaberaba. "Ainda não temos nada objetivo a informar (sobre suspensão de exportações)", afirmou o secretário-substituto de Comércio e Relações Internacionais do ministério, Rafael Requião. Ele disse ainda que o Brasil está analisando os protocolos para identificar quais medidas serão tomadas para um eventual "autoembargo" de exportações. "Não queremos antecipar a reação de parceiros, as discussões com a China começam agora", disse Requião. Não estava imediatamente claro se eventuais embargos poderiam atingir exportações de carne de peru ou de frango também. Requião disse ainda que o governo tem trabalhado com protocolos sanitários que permitem a "regionalização" do problema, o que evitaria embargos mais abrangentes sobre a carne brasileira. O ministro disse que nenhuma ave saiu da granja com registro da doença desde que as investigações começaram. As medidas de controle, contenção e erradicação do foco serão executadas conforme as diretrizes do Plano de Contingência para Influenza Aviária e Doença de Newcastle, disse o ministério. O estabelecimento Nova Itaberaba foi interditado pelo Serviço Veterinário Oficial, com suspensão da movimentação de aves. Já o secretário de Defesa Agropecuária substituto, Allan Alvarenga, afirmou que a doença não representa riscos à população. Ele acrescentou que a Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal foi notificada do caso no domingo. Apesar da necessidade de adoção de "medidas sanitárias para controlar a ocorrência, o consumo de produtos avícolas submetidos à inspeção oficial permanece seguro, sem contraindicações", ressaltou o ministério, em nota. Associações de produtores, como ABPA, ACAV e Sindicarne, destacaram em nota que a ocorrência de Doença de Newcastle não apresentou "manifestação clínica". Ou seja, houve a detecção do vírus, mas não da doença nos animais confinados.

item.title: Anthropic monta fundo "de benefício público” e Musk promete doar ações a crianças dos EUA
item.description: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do chatbot Claude, anunciou no domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público para facilitar doações em prol do “bem comum”, enquanto Elon Musk se comprometeu a doar uma ação da SpaceX a “cada criança nos Estados Unidos”.
item.dc:creator: Abu Sultan, Deborah Sophia
item.content:encoded: A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do chatbot Claude, anunciou no domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público para facilitar doações em prol do “bem comum”, enquanto Elon Musk se comprometeu a doar uma ação da SpaceX a “cada criança nos Estados Unidos”. A Anthropic informou que o fundo será constituído como uma sociedade de responsabilidade limitada de propriedade integral e receberá 2% adicionais das ações da companhia, a critério do conselho de administração, para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base que ainda não foi divulgada. A decisão dará à empresa mais flexibilidade e escala para fazer doações em benefício da humanidade, afirmou a companhia. A empresa está planejando uma das maiores ofertas públicas iniciais (IPOs) de ações da história como uma corporação de benefício público, uma estrutura jurídica que exige que a administração equilibre interesses públicos mais amplos com metas de lucratividade. Musk respondeu a uma publicação da Anthropic na rede social anunciando o fundo, dizendo que recomenda “doar as ações diretamente ao público”. “No ano que vem, darei uma das minhas ações da SpaceX para cada criança nos Estados Unidos. Essa será a primeira de muitas”, disse Musk, que dirige a SpaceXSI, rival da Anthropic, nesta segunda-feira. O bilionário detinha cerca de 6,42 bilhões de ações da empresa em junho. As ações da SpaceX (SPCX.O) subiram 2,5% no início do pregão desta segunda-feira. Dados do censo dos EUA mostram que há 72 milhões de crianças nos Estados Unidos; se uma única ação da SpaceX fosse distribuída a cada uma delas ao preço atual de negociação de US$149 cada, isso equivaleria a mais de US$10,7 bilhões. IMPACTO NO TRABALHO A Anthropic, que se posiciona como uma empresa de IA que prioriza a segurança, afirmou que a IA poderá representar “riscos catastróficos ou existenciais para a humanidade” e dedicou cerca de 80 páginas do corpo principal de seu prospecto de IPO, que tem 261 páginas, à exposição dos fatores de risco. A empresa afirmou em seu blog que o Fundo de Benefício Público poderá apoiar iniciativas que incluem doações para organizações sem fins lucrativos, distribuições diretas a populações específicas e esforços para lidar com o impacto da IA no mercado de trabalho. A Anthropic está se preparando para uma estreia na bolsa que poderá avaliá-la em cerca de US$2 trilhões, embora a Reuters tenha noticiado com exclusividade na semana passada que alguns investidores estejam considerando uma avaliação menor, de cerca de US$1,5 trilhão. Isso dará à participação de 5% no fundo um valor entre US$75 bilhões e US$100 bilhões. A Anthropic citou o impacto potencial da IA sobre os trabalhadores como uma das áreas de foco do novo fundo, com base em um compromisso de US$200 milhões anunciado anteriormente para estudar e lidar com as mudanças no mercado de trabalho. Uma pesquisa do FMI mostra que cerca de 40% dos empregos serão aprimorados, rebaixados ou eliminados pela IA, com esse número chegando a 60% nas economias avançadas, afirmou a diretora-geral Kristalina Georgieva na semana passada. DOAÇÕES POLÍTICAS? A Anthropic afirmou que nenhuma participação acionária detida por seu fundo será utilizada para lobby ou doações políticas nos EUA ou no exterior. Somado ao compromisso dos cofundadores de doar 80% de suas participações acionárias e a um programa de contrapartida de doações dos funcionários, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic serão destinadas a fins públicos, excluindo quaisquer ações adicionais que venham a ser incorporadas posteriormente. A Anthropic informou que divulgará mais detalhes nos próximos meses sobre a governança do fundo, sua estrutura e os limites de avaliação que poderiam ampliar sua participação. A empresa também planeja publicar um relatório detalhando o progresso em direção à sua missão.

item.title: Mulher afirma em tribunal do Reino Unido que comediante Russell Brand a estuprou
item.description: Uma mulher relatou à polícia que o ator e comediante britânico Russell Brand teria agarrado seus seios antes de arrastá-la para um banheiro de um bar e praticar estupro oral nela, segundo depoimento exibido em um tribunal de Londres nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden
item.content:encoded: Uma mulher relatou à polícia que o ator e comediante britânico Russell Brand teria agarrado seus seios antes de arrastá-la para um banheiro de um bar e praticar estupro oral nela, segundo depoimento exibido em um tribunal de Londres nesta segunda-feira. Brand, que já foi um dos apresentadores de maior destaque do Reino Unido e é ex-marido da cantora norte-americana Katy Perry, está sendo julgado sob acusação de três crimes de estupro, três de agressão sexual e um de agressão indecente contra seis mulheres entre 1999 e 2009. O homem de 51 anos nega as acusações e disse à polícia, após sua prisão, que nunca se envolveu em atividade sexual não consensual e que as denunciantes poderiam ter reimaginado os acontecimentos. A terceira das seis denunciantes a prestar depoimento alegou que Brand a havia agredido depois que ela o conheceu em uma festa em um bar de Londres, em 2004. “BRAND TINHA UM SORRISO ESTRANHO” Em um depoimento à polícia, dado em lágrimas e exibido aos jurados no Tribunal da Coroa de Southwark, a mulher, que trabalhava para a MTV, disse que queria conhecer Brand porque o tinha visto na televisão e achava que ele era muito engraçado. Mas, menos de um minuto depois de conversar com ele no bar, segundo ela, ele a agrediu. “Ele literalmente agarrou meus seios no meio da conversa”, disse ela, acrescentando que ele tinha um sorriso estranho e maníaco no rosto enquanto fazia isso. Imediatamente depois, enquanto ela estava em choque e sem acreditar no que estava acontecendo, ela disse que ele agarrou seu braço e a puxou para os banheiros que ficavam nas proximidades. Foi lá que ele supostamente a estuprou oralmente. “Aconteceu tão rápido”, ela contou à polícia. “Ele disse ‘vamos lá, vamos lá, não seja desmancha-prazeres’”, ela relatou, dizendo que ele a segurava à força pela cabeça e pelos cabelos. “Eu simplesmente congelei. Não sabia o que fazer.” Ela disse que, embora as palavras dele não fossem ameaçadoras, a força do ataque e o olhar dele sim. Ela rejeitou a sugestão do advogado de Brand, Ian Winter, de que ela teria ficado muito animada ao conhecê-lo, dizendo que “não estava impressionada com a celebridade... Eu não era uma colegial boba”. Winter argumentou que, se ela tivesse sido apalpada no bar ou arrastada para o banheiro, as pessoas teriam visto. “Vamos deixar claro que ele não fez isso com você”, disse ele sobre a suposta agressão sexual. “Você acompanhou alegremente o Sr. Brand até o banheiro”, acrescentou ele, sugestão que ela rejeitou. Ele afirmou que o suposto incidente no banheiro era “fisicamente impossível e não aconteceu”. Winter também questionou por que ela nunca havia dito que havia sido estuprada até depois de um documentário de 2023 e de uma reportagem na imprensa sobre Brand, tendo contado a amigos e à irmã que ele havia tentado se impor a ela, mas que ela havia conseguido fugir. “Eu não queria que as pessoas me julgassem... Eu sentia vergonha”, disse ela. Na semana passada, a primeira denunciante disse ao tribunal que Brand a havia estuprado depois que ela o conheceu em um evento paralelo à conferência do Partido Trabalhista de 1999, no sul da Inglaterra. A segunda das denunciantes contou ao Tribunal da Coroa de Southwark, em Londres, que, em 2001, um Brand com “olhos descontrolados” tentou arrastá-la para o banheiro masculino da MTV Europe, em Londres, onde ela trabalhava. O julgamento, que deve durar cerca de seis semanas, continua.

item.title: Eagles quarterback Hurts set to miss rest of season due to blood clots
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent said on Monday, and media reports said the former Super Bowl MVP was expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season. The Eagles announced on Thursday that Hurts had a superficial blood clot in his calf. Medical experts have evaluated him over the past few days. "Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli," the Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn said in a statement. The Eagles played in London on October 11, losing 19-17 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. A bilateral pulmonary embolism is where a blood clot travels from a deep vein in the body, often the leg, and blocks an artery in both lungs. Hurts guided the Eagles to the Super Bowl title in February 2025, throwing for two touchdowns and running in another against the Kansas City Chiefs to earn the game's Most Valuable Player trophy. He is clinically stable and his treatment should only involve blood thinners, which will rule him out of contact activities, the statement said. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the statement said, adding no long-term effects are expected.

item.title: Russian attack kills six at park in Kharkiv region, including three children, Ukraine says
item.description: A Russian drone attack on Monday killed six people, including three children, in a park in a village in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Russian drone attack on Monday killed six people, including three children, in a park in a village in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said. Syniehubov, writing on Telegram, had earlier said 15 people were injured in the strike southwest of the city of Kharkiv. The drone hit a park where families were playing with children, Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said. Vyhivskyi shared a blurred photo showing a child's body in a stroller. Other pictures posted online showed emergency crews working around a damaged building.

item.title: Oregon leading WR Evan Stewart facing DUII charge
item.description: Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested this weekend on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants, according to ABC affiliate KATU of Portland, Ore.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested this weekend on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants, according to ABC affiliate KATU of Portland, Ore. According to the report, Stewart was booked by police in Springfield, Ore., early Sunday morning and later released. He leads the Ducks in receptions (27) and receiving yards (352) and is tied for the team lead with four touchdown catches. The school had not commented on the matter as of Monday morning. A senior from Memphis, Tenn., Stewart did not play in Saturday's 17-14 home win against Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. The Ducks (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) return to action this Saturday on the road against Illinois (3-3, 1-2). Stewart has 166 catches for 2,128 yards and 15 touchdowns in 36 career games with Texas A&M (2022-23) and Oregon (2024, 2026). He missed the entire 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon. --Field Level Media

item.title: Canadian firms' outlooks dimmed after trade talks collapse, BoC survey finds
item.description: By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: By Promit Mukherjee and David Ljunggren OTTAWA, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Canadian firms reported their outlooks had deteriorated after the collapse of trade talks with the United States but sentiments remained considerably stronger than at the peak of tensions last year, the Bank of Canada said on Monday. A survey of around 340 business leaders in September showed that since the talks broke down on August 21, new US tariffs and Canadian counter tariffs had weighed on their outlooks. The bank said this suggested "a moderation rather than a fundamental shift in firms' outlooks". A separate Business Outlook Survey for the third quarter, which was largely carried out before the talks collapsed, showed overall sentiment had improved. But both surveys pointed to higher inflation expectations amid increase input costs and elevated selling prices due to trade tensions and the Middle East crisis. The studies help the BoC decide the trajectory of inflation and feed into its decision for the monetary policy. Money markets are pricing in a hold in interest rates by the BoC on October 28, but see a 25 basis point rise in December. Governor Tiff Macklem says while headline inflation has risen, this is primarily due by higher energy costs and there are so far no signs of a spillover into other components. But he also says he is ready to hike rates if higher prices show signs of feeding into the broader economy. The leaders' survey reported weaker export sales, the BoC said, adding that the improving sentiment at the beginning of the third quarter had partially reversed. "Nevertheless, sentiment and expectations remain considerably stronger than at the height of trade tensions in 2025," it added. In the Business Outlook Survey, the central bank said while there were some improvements in demand, firms' hiring intentions remained soft, but most firms intend to retain existing employees. Expectations for wage growth are largely unchanged, the survey noted. The business outlook indicator, a metric of prospects under current economic conditions, edged up to -0.33 in the third quarter from -0.38 in the prior three months. A separate survey by the central bank on consumer expectations showed that more than 50% of consumers surveyed expect a recession over the next 12 months and expectations for five-year inflation had also risen. ((Reuters Ottawa bureau)) Keywords: CANADA CENBANK/

item.title: Israel to resume commercial shipments to Gaza after Hamas fee dispute
item.description: Israel said on Monday it would resume allowing commercial goods shipments into Gaza after a days-long halt over a tax dispute involving Hamas and merchants, restoring a key route for food and other essentials to the aid-dependent enclave.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel said on Monday it would resume allowing commercial goods shipments into Gaza after a days-long halt over a tax dispute involving Hamas and merchants, restoring a key route for food and other essentials to the aid-dependent enclave. COGAT, the Israeli military agency overseeing humanitarian affairs in Gaza, said it made the decision after [USN:L8N4611UU TEXT:"merchants"] reported that Hamas authorities had withdrawn demands for payments of 10,000 shekels ($3,225) per truck. "The resumption of coordination is being carried out in accordance with Israel's commitment to the humanitarian provisions of the ceasefire agreement," it said. COGAT said the merchants' accounts had not been independently verified and shipments would resume gradually, with priority given to essential goods ahead of winter. Oversight would be tightened to ensure payments are made and received only through documented bank transfers, with any merchant found to have paid Hamas facing exclusion from the system. Hamas said the 10,000-shekel fee was a voluntary contribution by better-off Gazans to a national fund supporting people in need in the war-ravaged territory. Most Gazans remain dependent on aid after three years of war, repeated displacement and severe restrictions on aid deliveries . While last year's US-brokered ceasefire halted the heaviest fighting, it has not ended Israeli attacks. Local health officials said on Monday that at least five Palestinians, including a 14-year-old boy, were killed in separate Israeli strikes in Gaza City and Khan Younis. The Israeli military did not immediately comment. Israel says Hamas has continued to rearm and carry out attacks in violation of the ceasefire, while Hamas accuses Israel of undermining the agreement. Gaza health officials say about 1,500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire, while Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period. ($1 = 3.0991 shekels)

item.title: Egypt delays vote on military support for Saudi Arabia until October 26
item.description: Egypt's parliament delayed until October 26 a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, extending deliberations over a potentially deeper Egyptian role in the conflict with Yemen's Houthis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Egypt's parliament delayed until October 26 a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, extending deliberations over a potentially deeper Egyptian role in the conflict with Yemen's Houthis. Members of the House of Representatives said it adjourned a second closed-door session on Monday, held to discuss President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request for authority to take measures [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"to support the kingdom"] following recent attacks. Egypt's constitution requires a two-thirds parliamentary majority to approve sending its armed forces on a combat mission beyond the country's borders, after consultation with the National Defence Council. Sisi said on [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"Saturday"] that Egypt would take "any measure" necessary to protect Gulf allies, marking a sharper public commitment after Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure. The Egyptian Social Democratic Party said on Sunday it had instructed its lawmakers to abstain, saying parliament had not received sufficient information about the proposed mission's objectives, scope, duration, cost or risks to Egyptian troops. While affirming support for Saudi security, the party said Egypt should avoid an open-ended military commitment and preserve room for diplomacy, citing the country's economic pressures and the risks to Red Sea shipping and Suez Canal revenue. Al-Azhar's grand imam also called on Sunday for an urgent mediation effort by Arab and Muslim leaders to contain the conflict and avert further bloodshed. The issue underscores Cairo's close security and financial ties with Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has a $5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month, plus $267.39 million in interest, central bank data showed. Egypt's EGX30 index, which fell early in the session amid concern over possible military involvement, recovered to close 0.4% higher. Nematallah Choucri, head of research at HC Securities, said geopolitical developments had become the main factor behind recent market losses.

item.title: Reports: Falcons signing Andy Dalton, cutting Cooper Rush
item.description: The Atlanta Falcons are signing veteran Andy Dalton and releasing fellow quarterback Cooper Rush, according to multiple media reports Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Falcons are signing veteran Andy Dalton and releasing fellow quarterback Cooper Rush, according to multiple media reports Monday. Dalton, who turns 39 on Oct. 29, was released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 9 after throwing an interception on his only pass attempt of the season in a Week 3 loss at Chicago. Since playing his first nine seasons and making three Pro Bowls with the Cincinnati Bengals from 2011-19, Dalton has played for the Dallas Cowboys, Bears, New Orleans Saints, Carolina Panthers and Eagles. Rush started the Falcons' first two games this season as Michael Penix Jr. completed his recovery from ACL surgery, losing to the Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers. Atlanta (2-4) also has veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and undrafted rookie Jack Strand on the roster. Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards with 254 touchdowns and 152 interceptions across 180 career games, compiling a record of 84-83-2 as a starter in the regular season. Rush, 32, completed 22 of 39 passes for 229 yards with one TD and four picks this season. He was a longtime backup with the Dallas Cowboys before making two starts last season for the Baltimore Ravens. --Field Level Media

item.title: Second-hand clothing app Vinted purges suspected stolen goods after France riots
item.description: Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest in France.
item.dc:creator: Anna Peverieri
item.content:encoded: Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest in France. Nationwide demonstrations across France over the cost of living and declining public service [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"deteriorated into riots"] on Saturday, with shops looted across the country as violent groups clashed with police in one of the worst days of violence in years. Vinted said its teams had taken "immediate action" since the weekend to identify and remove listings suspected of being linked to looting, and had increased scrutiny of suspicious adverts. Accounts found to have breached its rules could face permanent bans, it said. "The sale of stolen goods, or soliciting them, is strictly prohibited on Vinted, and we have zero tolerance for it," a Vinted spokesperson said in a statement. The company said it was working with law enforcement and French authorities and would continue to adapt its processes to identify and counter emerging risks and malicious behaviour. Serge Papin, France's small businesses minister, said on X that authorities would meet later in the day with marketplace operators and officials from the interior and justice ministries, after goods stolen during Saturday's unrest were offered for sale online. Platforms including Vinted, Amazon, eBay and TikTok were invited to the meeting on Monday, according to government officials. Vinted did not say whether it had seen a similar increase in suspicious listings in [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"Italy"], where unrest also led to the looting of luxury stores. France, the UK and Italy are Vinted's largest markets. [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"Luxury groups"] including Louis Vuitton (LVMH.PA) and Rolex, as well as make-up retail giant Sephora, have been caught up in unrest in [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"France"] and [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"Italy"] where some of the most violent protests seen in decades over living costs and declining public services have prompted police to fire tear gas and use water cannon as demonstrators looted shops and set fires. Founded in Lithuania in 2008, Vinted became the Baltic state's first "unicorn" - a startup valued at €1 billion - in 2019. A secondary share transaction led by Sweden's EQT Growth [USN:L4N41A19T TEXT:"valued Vinted at €8 billion"] earlier this year. The online marketplace prohibits the sale of stolen items and relies on reports from retailers and users, among other checks, to detect suspicious listings.

item.title: UK's Doncaster Sheffield Airport set for public ownership ahead of reopening
item.description: Britain's Doncaster Sheffield Airport, which closed almost four years ago but handled more than 1.4 million passengers in 2019, looks set to return to public ownership with a view to reopening next year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Doncaster Sheffield Airport, which closed almost four years ago but handled more than 1.4 million passengers in 2019, looks set to return to public ownership with a view to reopening next year. South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority on Monday said its mayor and regional leaders were set approve a deal to buy the airport, and adjacent land called the Innovation Quarter, from current owners Peel Land. • SYMCA plans to restore freight services from autumn 2027 and passenger services from spring 2028, subject to regulatory and operational work needed to reopen the airport • The deal needs formal approval from the boards of SYMCA and Peel Land • Last year SYMCA approved about £160 million ($213 million)of funding for the reopening • SYMCA did not immediately disclose how much it would pay Peel. A report to its board said the deal was "not without risk" to the taxpayer, but recommended approval • SYMCA would become freehold owner of the site • The South Yorkshire region, home to Boeing's first European factory, seeks to make the airport area a hub for sustainable aviation and advanced manufacturing • Peel closed the airport in November 2022, saying it had never made a profit, after Wizz Air pulled its based aircraft. Peel rejected an offer of public money to cover losses for a year • The reopening has been repeatedly delayed. As recently as February 2025, local authorities were targeting passenger flights by spring 2026 ($1 = 0.7512 pounds)

item.title: Rendimientos de bonos Tesoro EEUU suben levemente mientras disminuyen temores sobre la IA
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU subían ligeramente el lunes y el retorno de los bonos a 10 años se recuperaba tras su mayor caída semanal en siete meses, mientras se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre el impacto del aumento de las tasas de interés en las acciones del sector de la IA.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de EEUU subían ligeramente el lunes y el retorno de los bonos a 10 años se recuperaba tras su mayor caída semanal en siete meses, mientras se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre el impacto del aumento de las tasas de interés en las acciones del sector de la IA. * El rendimiento a 10 años cayó 14,6 puntos básicos la semana pasada, incluso tras conocerse unos datos de inflación más altos de lo esperado, reflejados en el índice de precios al consumo y el índice de precios al productor. * Los mercados bursátiles sufrieron una corrección debido a la preocupación de que las inversiones en acciones de infraestructuras de IA pudieran empezar a agotarse, lo que potenció el atractivo de los bonos del Tesoro como valor refugio. * Sin embargo, las acciones subían en las primeras horas de negociación del lunes, gracias a la recuperación de los valores relacionados con la IA, mientras que el descenso de los precios del petróleo también contribuía a mitigar los temores inflacionarios. * El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años subía 0,8 puntos básicos, al 5,106%. El rendimiento del bono a 30 años subía 1,2 puntos básicos, al 5,447%. * Un segmento muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, que mide la diferencia entre el retorno de la deuda a dos y a diez años —y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas—, se situaba en 35,3 puntos básicos positivos. * Esta semana llegará más oferta al mercado cuando el Tesoro subaste el miércoles 13.000 millones de dólares en bonos a 20 años y el jueves 26.000 millones de dólares en Títulos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos protegidos contra la inflación (TIPS) a 5 años . * El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subía 1,3 puntos básicos al 4,749%. * Las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas al menos 25 puntos básicos en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana se sitúan en el 17,2%, según el CME FedWatch, lo que supone un descenso respecto al 21% de hace una semana y al 57,6% de hace un mes.

item.title: South Africa must prepare for potential loss of US trade benefits, president says
item.description: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Monday that the country must prepare for its potential exclusion from the United States' duty-free trade initiative, AGOA, as relations between Washington and Pretoria have soured.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Monday that the country must prepare for its potential exclusion from the United States' duty-free trade initiative, AGOA, as relations between Washington and Pretoria have soured. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US market for thousands of products. South Africa has benefited from it for years. President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:S0N43F07R TEXT:"cracked down on"] South Africa for what Trump claims is its persecution of white people. South Africa's government says this is a falsehood spread by fringe groups. Ramaphosa said it remained to be seen whether South Africa would remain part of AGOA and his government was in discussions with US counterparts. Some US officials have suggested [USN:S0N3XA08H TEXT:"South Africa should be excluded"]. "I need, as president, to prepare us if it ever happens," Ramaphosa said. He said the impact on jobs would be "devastating" and he and Deputy President Paul Mashatile have been travelling around the world to explore alternative markets. Ramaphosa cited a recent trade agreement with China as a positive step. China introduced a zero-tariff scheme for qualifying South African goods in May.

item.title: Carney says cause of fire at Alberta military base still unknown
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday that the cause of a firethat killed at least four military members and injured dozens of others in Alberta on Saturday is still unknown.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday that the cause of a fire that killed at least four military members and injured dozens of others in Alberta on Saturday is still unknown. Carney said in an address to Parliament that soldiers and reserve members were conducting live-fire exercises at an army base in Wainwright while a fire was burning in the training area. “Driven by ferocious winds, the fire jumped nearly a kilometer in less than a minute to where soldiers were gathered,” Carney said. He added that 50 investigators are currently on the ground, from the army and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, to determine how the disaster happened. "This loss touches every corner of the nation," Carney said. Officials said 39 people remain hospitalized, with 19 people in critical condition. The soldiers and reserve members were preparing to deploy to Latvia, where Canadian forces have their largest international military operation. Kent Moore, a professor of atmospheric physics at the University of Toronto, said the embers from grass fires in dry conditions can spread incredibly quickly. He said there didn't appear to be any rain in the area, so it was unlikely the fire was triggered by lightning. "The fact that the winds were so strong suggests to me that it wouldn't have taken much to start this fire," he said, speculating that it was likely caused by human error, including sparks from vehicles or live fire, or an errant cigarette from a smoker.

item.title: Trump creará nueva división de Institutos Nacionales de Salud y grupo de trabajo para salud de la mujer
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, firmará este lunes, junto a la primera dama, Melania Trump, un decreto presidencial mediante el cual se creará un grupo de trabajo y una división de los Institutos Nacionales de Salud (NIH, por sus siglas en inglés) dedicada a la salud de la mujer, según ha informado la Casa Blanca.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, firmará este lunes, junto a la primera dama, Melania Trump, un decreto presidencial mediante el cual se creará un grupo de trabajo y una división de los Institutos Nacionales de Salud (NIH, por sus siglas en inglés) dedicada a la salud de la mujer, según ha informado la Casa Blanca. El grupo de trabajo estará dirigido por la jefa de gabinete de Trump en la Casa Blanca, Susie Wiles —quien anunció recientemente que ya no padece cáncer— y por el secretario de Salud, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., según dijo un funcionario de la Casa Blanca. La nueva División de Salud de la Mujer de los NIH no sustituirá a la Oficina de Investigación sobre la Salud de la Mujer de la agencia, sino que tendrá un mandato más amplio que irá más allá de la investigación. "El presidente Donald J. Trump y la primera dama Melania Trump firmarán un decreto ejecutivo por el que se crea una División de Salud de la Mujer en los NIH y un Grupo de Trabajo de la Casa Blanca sobre la Salud de la Mujer, con el objetivo de subsanar las lagunas en la investigación y modernizar la atención sanitaria para las mujeres", indicó una publicación en la red social X en la que se anunció la firma. No fue posible contactar de inmediato con representantes del Departamento de Salud y Servicios Humanos, que supervisa los NIH, para recabar sus comentarios. La noticia de la orden la publicó por primera vez USA Today. En el discurso previsto para el acto, se espera que Melania Trump aborde la necesidad de utilizar la inteligencia artificial para acelerar los avances en materia de salud de la mujer, así como el acceso a la atención sanitaria y su asequibilidad, según indicó el funcionario. Trump y su administración han impulsado recortes en salud, incluso en los NIH, y el año pasado tomaron medidas para reducir la plantilla sanitaria federal. Durante el segundo mandato de Trump, su administración intentó recortar las subvenciones de los NIH destinadas a la investigación sobre asuntos relacionados con la diversidad y, según se informa, está tomando medidas para permitir que los cargos políticos controlen la financiación de la investigación sanitaria.

item.title: France in turmoil: What might follow a weekend of riots?
item.description: France saw some of the worst unrest in years at the weekend as huge protests across the country over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France saw some of the worst [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"unrest in years"] at the weekend as huge protests across the country over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting. Limoges town hall was torched and more than 3,000 shops were pillaged or damaged, according to the government, as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. While mayors of France's biggest cities [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"demanded answers"] from the government on Monday over what they say was a lack of preparation, authorities rushed to set up support measures for impacted businesses and bolster security as calm returned to the streets. Here is the latest on the situation in France: WHAT WILL THE GOVERNMENT DO TO QUELL THE VIOLENCE, COMPENSATE VICTIMS? Some 2,400 people were arrested during the weekend and police investigators are poring over online videos and images to track down looters. [USN:L8N4650PE TEXT:"Partial curfews"] are being organised in some municipalities while the government has said it will increase police numbers on the ground, especially for next weekend if it sees renewed protests. It has not specified how many extra officers will be made available. For businesses and victims of the violence, the government is putting in place state-financed furlough measures to help employers avoid layoffs, and funds are being set aside to help companies meet their immediate cashflow needs. The government has yet to provide full details of the funding or how the money will be distributed. Insurers are also expected to cover some of the damage. HOW WILL THE GOVERNMENT ADDRESS COMPLAINTS ABOUT THE COST OF LIVING AND PUBLIC SERVICES? France's extremely strained public finances mean the government has precious little room for broader measures to address protesters' anger over the rising cost of living. It has already hiked emergency spending this year to help certain sectors like farmers, fishermen and haulers cope with high fuel costs caused by the Iran war . The protests in France [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"began last month at high schools"] in Paris' working-class northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement. The government has so far not committed to a substantial increase in funding for schools. However, it [USN:L6N45V0FM TEXT:"has pledged"] to send some 3,000 teachers, who are fully qualified but have not yet started work, to fill staffing gaps. WILL PROTESTS ESCALATE OR HAVE THEY PEAKED? Some protesters have already called for a new round of demonstrations on Saturday, October 24. Unions have called for strikes on November 5 to protest budget cuts and support hiking wages. The weekend violence has largely eclipsed the recent high school student protests. Schools are now on a break for two weeks, but there have been reports of protests at some universities. HOW WILL THE CRISIS AFFECT FRANCE'S DIRE ECONOMIC SITUATION? The unrest will likely deal a blow to business confidence, which is already fragile due to a fiscal crisis and high energy prices resulting from the Iran war. The minority government is struggling to pass spending cuts in France's deeply divided parliament as part of its 2027 budget and is at risk of being toppled by opposition parties if a compromise cannot be found with at least some of them. The unrest has weighed on French stocks and the euro and put pressure on [USN:L1N465097 TEXT:"French government bonds"], pushing the risk premium over the 10-year German benchmark up to 146 basis points, the highest in two weeks. WILL THE UNREST SPREAD TO OTHER COUNTRIES? If France cannot contain the unrest, there is a risk that it could spill across its borders. In neighbouring Italy, [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"clashes erupted"] between police and protesters on Sunday during demonstrations over poor public services and the rising cost of living. Albania has also seen a series of student demonstrations in recent days over corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards while Spain and Portugal have faced protests over housing. HOW WILL THE UNREST AFFECT THE 2027 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION? Elections next year will see President Emmanuel Macron step down after a decade in power. The unrest is likely to give a boost to far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in polls to replace him and has long talked tough on law and order. "Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, a former lawmaker from Macron's camp, [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"told Reuters"]. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her, it's a six-lane highway." Hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has come under pressure for backing protesters' demands, criticising the government's handling and not clearly condemning the violence. Meanwhile, Macron, who headed off to the Middle East on Monday, has emerged from the crisis further weakened. His former prime minister Edouard Philippe, now a centre-right presidential candidate, said on X he wanted "decisions and initiatives" from the lame-duck leader to "restore order". ARE PARIS AND OTHER CITIES SAFE TO VISIT? There have been no reports of any injuries to foreigners caught up in the unrest. However, several European governments [USN:L8N4650JR TEXT:"advised citizens"] travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution.

item.title: Paul Mackenzie, the Kenyan preacher who led hundreds to starve to death
item.description: More than three years after Kenyan police unearthed mass graves linked to a starvation cult led by evangelist Paul Mackenzie, the preacher was convicted of murder for the deaths of 190 children and one adult.
item.dc:creator: Ammu Kannampilly
item.content:encoded: More than three years after Kenyan police [USN:L8N3TR154 TEXT:"unearthed mass graves"] linked to a starvation cult led by evangelist Paul Mackenzie, the preacher was [USN:L8N4651FW TEXT:"convicted of murder"] for the deaths of 190 children and one adult. Mackenzie's case has gripped the East African nation since officers found human remains in a forest near the Indian Ocean town of Malindi in April 2023, kicking off an investigation that would eventually unearth over 400 bodies, nearly half of them children. The former taxi driver founded the Good News International Church in 2003, preaching increasingly apocalyptic sermons and [USN:L8N3UL0KV TEXT:"urging his followers to starve themselves"] and their children to death so they could go to heaven before the world ended. In a March 2023 YouTube video, Mackenzie — who had thousands of followers in person and online — said that he was guided by "the voice of Christ" when he preached messages about the world coming to an end that year. "I followed the voice that told me I had finished the work," he said. PRESIDENT HAS SAID DEATHS SHOULD HAVE BEEN PREVENTED Videos of the preacher show him dressed in nondescript clothing, speaking calmly to hundreds of people as he recounted his experiences as an exorcist and his victory over "demonic" spirits. Mackenzie denied charges of murder, manslaughter, child torture and terrorism in a case that highlighted the failings of Kenyan authorities and the lack of oversight governing churches in the predominantly Christian country. The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights, an independent body, said it was deplorable that Mackenzie could have been first arrested in 2017 and charged with radicalisation but continued to operate for years. "This points to a failure in the investigation and prosecution processes. The arrest should have triggered investigations that would have saved the lives of several people," the KNCHR said in a 2024 report. Kenyan President William Ruto has said that government agencies should have been able to prevent the deaths, adding that he took responsibility as president. DOZENS OF CHILDREN FOUND LIVING IN COMPOUND Mackenzie grew up in Kwale, a rural county in southeast Kenya, and moved to Malindi in the early 1990s to work as a taxi driver. There, he became increasingly focused on religion, Japheth Charo, who worked as a driver alongside him, told Reuters in 2023. "He started attacking other faiths like Muslims and Catholics. His preaching started becoming extreme," said Charo, whose family had joined Mackenzie's church but left after his sermons started to alarm them. In 2012, Mackenzie registered a TV company called Good News Media and he broadcast sermons on a YouTube channel that had 7,000 subscribers, KNCHR wrote in a report on the case. Police searched Mackenzie's Malindi compound in 2017 and found dozens of children living there without attending school. He was charged with offering education at an unregistered facility but continued his teachings until 2019, when his church was shut down and he relocated to the Shakahola Forest. People were lured there by the promise of affordable arable land but found armed militia who enforced the fasting and eventual deaths of followers, KNCHR found. Those who defied orders to fast or tried to escape were strangled or clubbed to death, it added. STARVE THEMSELVES BEFORE THE WORLD'S END Mackenzie, believed to be in his early 50s, is a domineering figure who forced his followers to cut themselves off from society, forbidding them from engaging with schools or hospitals, institutions he branded as satanic, relatives of victims said. "He told them to starve themselves ahead of the world's end on April 15, saying he would be the last one and that he would lock the doors," Stephen Mwiti, whose wife and six children were among the fatalities, told Reuters in 2023. Mackenzie's grip on his followers continued even after the graves in Shakahola were exposed. Prosecutors charged him in connection with the deaths of 52 other people after bodies were exhumed last year in Kwa Binzaro village, some 30 km (18 miles) from Shakahola. They said he masterminded and oversaw the offences at Kwa Binzaro while in detention, using radical teachings to draw victims to the remote site. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.

item.title: Tenista ucraniana Svitolina anuncia fim de casamento com Monfils e cita efeitos da guerra
item.description: A tenista número seis do mundo, Elina Svitolina, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que ela e o ex-tenista Gael Monfils estavam encerrando seu casamento, e a ucraniana acrescentou que o impacto emocional da guerra da Rússia em seu país a levou a sentir a necessidade de se redescobrir.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A tenista número seis do mundo, Elina Svitolina, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que ela e o ex-tenista Gael Monfils estavam encerrando seu casamento, e a ucraniana acrescentou que o impacto emocional da guerra da Rússia em seu país a levou a sentir a necessidade de se redescobrir. Eles se casaram em julho de 2021 e tiveram uma filha, Skai, em outubro de 2022. Ao anunciar a separação em uma postagem no Instagram, Svitolina descreveu as dificuldades pessoais que vem enfrentando desde a invasão russa à Ucrânia em 2022 e o impacto que elas tiveram em sua vida fora das quadras de tênis. “Esta é a coisa mais difícil que já tive que compartilhar”, escreveu Svitolina. “Todos sabem o quanto a Ucrânia significa para mim. O que raramente falei é o que a guerra causou em mim por dentro." “No ano passado, eu disse a vocês que precisava me afastar das quadras porque não estava no estado emocional adequado. Hoje, quero me abrir um pouco mais. O que vocês não viram foram as noites sem dormir, as dúvidas e a sensação de estar me perdendo aos poucos." “Gael viu tudo isso. Ele nunca soltou minha mão. Lutamos juntos contra isso por muito tempo, com tudo o que tínhamos. Mas algumas batalhas acontecem bem no fundo de você, e nenhum amor vindo de outra pessoa pode vencê-las por você”, completou. Svitolina pediu compreensão e respeito pela privacidade enquanto a família lida com a separação, ressaltando que não há ninguém a quem culpar. “Com o tempo, passei a entender que preciso reencontrar a mim mesma e que não posso fazer isso dentro do nosso casamento”, acrescentou a semifinalista de 32 anos do Aberto da Austrália. “É a verdade mais difícil que já tive de encarar e a coisa mais difícil que já tive de dizer à pessoa que amo." O francês Monfils, de 40 anos, ex-número seis do mundo e um dos jogadores mais carismáticos de sua geração, se aposentou do tênis profissional, de acordo com a Agência Internacional de Integridade do Tênis (ITIA). Ele planejava se aposentar no final de 2026 e se despedir no Masters de Paris, em novembro, mas a ITIA agora o lista como aposentado.

item.title: EEUU dice inmigrantes de Ucrania y Sudán pueden conservar su estatus de protección por el momento
item.description: Los inmigrantes procedentes de Ucrania y Sudán podrán mantener su estatus de protección temporal en Estados Unidos por el momento, informó el lunes el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, el mismo día en que estaba previsto que expiraran dichas protecciones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los inmigrantes procedentes de Ucrania y Sudán podrán mantener su estatus de protección temporal en Estados Unidos por el momento, informó el lunes el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, el mismo día en que estaba previsto que expiraran dichas protecciones. En un comunicado, un portavoz del DHS afirmó que los anuncios relativos a los titulares de TPS de Ucrania y Sudán "se harían en el momento oportuno" y que sus protecciones en materia de inmigración seguirían vigentes. El estatus de protección temporal permite a las personas que ya se encuentran en Estados Unidos permanecer en el país y trabajar legalmente si sus países de origen se ven afectados por desastres naturales, conflictos armados u otras circunstancias extraordinarias. Esta prórroga temporal es la segunda en otros tantos meses para determinados inmigrantes acogidos al programa del TPS, a pesar de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha tomado medidas para expulsar a otros ciudadanos extranjeros como parte de su agresiva campaña contra la inmigración. En septiembre, su Gobierno permitió a los beneficiarios del TPS procedentes de El Salvador conservar sus protecciones, tras haber tomado anteriormente medidas para revocarlas a haitianos, venezolanos, somalíes, yemeníes, sirios y otros. Esta última medida se produce en un momento en que Trump ha dejado de centrarse en Ucrania en los últimos días, negándose a imponer sanciones más duras a Rusia por la guerra que dura ya cuatro años y levantando las sanciones a las exportaciones de gasóleo de Moscú. Unos 240.000 ucranianos que huyeron del conflicto se han inscrito para obtener el estatus de TPS en Estados Unidos. Se estima que hay 6.800 beneficiarios del TPS procedentes de Sudán, donde una guerra entre el ejército y un grupo paramilitar rival ha provocado una de las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo.

item.title: Plaza cambiaria argentina se mantiene controlada con seguimiento de banco central
item.description: El mercado cambiario argentino operaba con una leve merma el lunes con el habitual control de la entidad monetaria local que regula la liquidez mediante compra o venta de divisas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El mercado cambiario argentino operaba con una leve merma el lunes con el habitual control de la entidad monetaria local que regula la liquidez mediante compra o venta de divisas. El Banco Central (BCRA) en las últimas jornadas ha incrementado su accionar en la plaza cambiaria, donde el viernes adquirió 68 millones de dólares y acumuló un saldo semanal positivo levemente superior a los 640 millones de dólares. Las compras de la entidad elevaron las "reservas internacionales brutas a 50.236 millones de dólares y completando un saldo semanal comprador de 642 millones de dólares, el monto más alto registrado en los últimos tres meses", expresó Wise Capital. "La estrategia oficial responde a la urgencia de abastecer de divisas al Tesoro de cara a los compromisos de deuda con tenedores de bonos Globales agendados para el próximo 9 de enero", añadió. En este contexto, el peso mayorista se depreciaba un 0,36% a 1.523,5 unidades por dólar para la venta. Por su parte, el riesgo país argentino se ubicaba en 660 puntos básicos, con los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil cayendo un leve 0,2% a las 1445 GMT. La secretaría de Finanzas, dependiente del Ministerio de Economía a cargo del Luis Caputo, anunció una conversión de títulos que se llevará a cabo el martes. "La operación permitirá a los tenedores del bono dollar-linked con vencimiento a fines de octubre (D30O6) canjearlo por instrumentos con vencimiento a fines de noviembre, en enero de 2027 y en junio de 2027.", afirmó la consultora Max Capital. Y añadió que "al igual que en anteriores vencimientos de instrumentos dollar-linked, el Tesoro ofrece un canje anticipado para reducir la potencial volatilidad cambiaria antes de la fijación del precio el 27 de octubre". El Índice accionario argentino, localmente conocido como Merval, desde el 19 de octubre pasará a conocerse como MSCI Merval tras el acuerdo entre Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (BYMA) y el proveedor global de índices MSCI. "Como te adelantamos al anunciar la alianza estratégica entre BYMA y MSCI (...) se lanzarán los nuevos índices de Renta Variable", dijo BYMA en un comunicado. Y agregó que entre algunas de las principales características con la que contarán los índices será un valor inicial de 100 mil pesos para ambos y una moneda de publicación que será en pesos argentinos y dólares estadounidenses. El nuevo índice accionario, el MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) iniciaba su primera jornada de negocios en baja.

item.title: Retailer Ahold Delhaize reports cybersecurity incident to Dutch police
item.description: Retailer Ahold Delhaize reported a cybersecurity incident to Dutch police on Monday after it detected suspicious activity in its infrastructure, the company said, adding it took some systems offline as a precaution earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Van Campenhout
item.content:encoded: Retailer Ahold Delhaize (AD.AS) reported a [USN:L8N45Z1DC TEXT:"cybersecurity incident"] to Dutch police on Monday after it detected suspicious activity in its infrastructure, the company said, adding it took some systems offline as a precaution earlier this month. Although only reported to the police on Monday, the incident coincided with a [USN:L8N45Y11U TEXT:"cyberattack in France"] that caused refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of stores to heat up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, sparking fires and spoiling food. The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre said there was no reason to believe the incident in the Netherlands was directly linked to any cyberattacks in other countries. Delhaize said its investigations found the suspicious activity had resulted from the "malicious actions of others", without specifying who might be responsible. "Taking systems offline to help protect them was a precautionary measure that affected most of our brands across Europe and the United States. The investigation to date confirms this was the right decision", President and CEO Frans Muller said. NO ONLINE ORDERS BEFORE THURSDAY Earlier on Monday, Ahold Delhaize's Albert Heijn, the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain, said it would [USN:L1N465082 TEXT:"not resume"] online deliveries before Thursday at the earliest, extending to at least 11 days an outage caused by the cybersecurity incident. Online accounts for about 10% of Albert Heijn sales. While Albert Heijn's website was back online on Monday, the websites of Ahold Delhaize’s US chains remained offline, a week after the cyber incident forced the company to shut down some of its IT systems. Ahold Delhaize said it expected e-commerce services at its US brands to resume "in the coming days". The US brands, which include Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Hannaford and Food Lion, collectively rank among the country’s largest food retailers. Deliveries at Belgian chain Delhaize resumed over the weekend. Ahold Delhaize previously said that there was no evidence that any customer data had been stolen. Physical stores of several chains have remained open, but have struggled with supplies as distribution channels were also affected.
