item.title: Apple faces new damages bid after landmark $5.7 billion patent verdict
item.description: A technology company that won a landmark $5.7 billion patent infringement verdict against Apple has asked a federal judge to tack on more damages and interest, potentially exposing the iPhone maker to hundreds of millions of dollars in additional liability.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A technology company that won a landmark $5.7 billion patent infringement verdict against Apple (AAPL.O) has asked a federal judge to tack on more damages and interest, potentially exposing the iPhone maker to hundreds of millions of dollars in additional liability. Here are the details: A California federal jury in September awarded San Diego-based Taction the largest-ever US patent infringement award after finding Apple [USN:L6N45I048 TEXT:"violated"] its patented technology for haptic feedback in iPhones and Apple Watches Taction in a filing on Friday said the verdict only covers Apple sales from 2021 to late March and asked the court to impose damages for the six months of sales since then Taction also asked the judge to award prejudgment interest at California's 7% statutory rate, which would add at least hundreds of millions of dollars to the $5.7 billion verdict “The size of the jury’s award is no reason to withhold interest,” Taction told the court. The company is also seeking post-judgment interest Apple has denied any wrongdoing and said it will appeal. It has also [USN:L6N4600XS TEXT:"asked the court"] to overturn the verdict Apple was ordered to pay $184.2 million in prejudgment interest to medical-monitoring technology company Masimo this month in a different intellectual property case after Masimo [USN:L6N3WF0PJ TEXT:"won a jury award"] of $634 million last year The case is Taction Technology v. Apple Inc, US District Court for the Southern District of California, No. 3:21-cv-00812. For Taction: Lance Yang of Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan For Apple: Roger Denning of Fish & Richardson Read more: [USN:L6N4600XS TEXT:"Apple asks US court to overturn jury's landmark $5.7 billion patent verdict"] [USN:L6N45I048 TEXT:"US jury says Apple owes record $5.7 billion in haptic technology patent case"]

item.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader convicted in deaths of nearly 200 children
item.description: A Kenyan court on Monday found starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of 190 children and one adult in one of the world's worst cult-related disasters in recent history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Kenyan court on Monday found starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of 190 children and one adult in one of the world's worst cult-related disasters in recent history. Mackenzie and his co-accused will be given their sentence on November 6. He was [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"arrested in 2023"] after police received a tip-off, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest near the coast in southeastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and his Good News International Church organised a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve, but the court rejected that argument. In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered from the Shakahola Forest. Many were severely decomposed, with only 26 bodies able to be identified. Monday's judgment covered 191 deaths while investigations into the other deaths are ongoing. FAMILIES IN COURT TO HEAR VERDICT Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched. Mackenzie was in court, wearing a striped polo shirt and red trousers, sitting alongside his wife who is one of the co-accused. When his name was read out by the judge he stood silently, staring into space. Family members of some of those who died in the forest gathered to hear the judgment at Mombasa High Court. Francis Wanje, 62, lost eight family members including two grandchildren to the cult. Speaking before the verdict, he told Reuters: "It has been really a heavy thing (for) us as a family, and it has really taken us very far in terms of psychological problems, ... I was hoping for this particular day." The Shakahola tragedy has gripped Kenya since the discovery of mass graves in the coastal forest more than three years ago. It raised questions over how Mackenzie was able to continue to operate despite having been on the radar of the authorities since 2017 when his premises were searched by police. In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie's church and he relocated to the Shakahola Forest, police said. The case has also led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life. Kenyan President William Ruto said in 2023 that government agencies should have been able to prevent the deaths. He said he took responsibility as president. CHILDREN WERE FIRST TO STARVE People with direct knowledge of the cult's activities [USN:L8N36W0BR TEXT:"told Reuters"] that Mackenzie planned the mass starvation in three phases: first children, then women and young men, and finally the remaining men. A former taxi driver, Mackenzie forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, branding such institutions as Satanic, some of his followers told Reuters for a 2023 article. Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names like Jerusalem and Judea. The plight of his followers began to emerge in mid-March 2023, when a local man told police that his brother and wife had starved their children to death in the forest on Mackenzie's orders. Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives say he brought forward the date on which he told his followers the world would end. Police arrested him again in April 2023 and started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves. Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths including terrorism-related ones, which he has denied. Prosecutors say while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"Kwa Binzaro village"], which lies about 30 km (18 miles) from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.

item.title: Europe EV sales rose 70% in September, around 30% of market share
item.description: Battery-electric vehicle (BEV) registrations in Europe rose 70.3% in September, as high oil prices, subsidies and the availability of more affordable models continued to lead the growth.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Battery-electric vehicle (BEV) registrations in Europe rose 70.3% in September, as high oil prices, subsidies and the availability of more affordable models continued to lead the growth. Around a third of cars sold across 17 key European markets in September were BEVs, data from E-Mobility Europe, New Automotive and Fier Automotive showed on Monday, amid a [USN:L6N4620KS TEXT:"deal "]made by France and Germany to soften proposed EU car emissions rules. BEV registrations reached 300,202 vehicles in September, giving fully electric cars a 32.6% market share 1.98 million BEVs have been registered across Europe so far this year, up 38.1% from the same period in 2025 France hit a 41.7% BEV market share with 65,243 registrations, while Germany's share reached 34.6% with 88,724 registrations. The Nordic market remained Europe's most electrified, led by Norway at 98.8% and followed by Denmark (88.8%), Finland (62.7%) and Sweden (49.0%). BEVs accounted for around half of the registrations in Ireland, Portugal, Belgium and the Netherlands The Czech Republic, Italy and Poland remained among Europe's least electrified markets at 11.2%, 7.6% and 6.2%, respectively. (This story has been corrected to say that the BEV market share is around 30%, not almost, in the headline and paragraph 2.)

item.title: 中国証監会、市場安定を最優先へ 株式や債券の動向注視＝国営メディア
item.description: [上海／北京 １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[上海／北京 １９日 ロイター] - 中国国営メディアは１９日、中国証券監督管理委員会（証監会）の呉清主席が北京で開かれた金融フォーラムで、資本市場の安定を最優先する方針を示したと報じた。株式や債券、為替市場でボラティリティーや相関性が高まっているとして、リスク評価や政策手段を強化すると表明した。

呉氏は、世界市場の関連性が強まっていることを踏まえ、証監会として国内外の市場を注視し、市場安定の仕組みを改善すると述べた。市場や部門を横断して波及するリスクに細心の注意を払う必要があると指摘。新たな業態などに伴うリスクへの備えを強化するほか、中国内の個別銘柄に連動するオフショアのレバレッジ商品に関しても警戒していくと言及した。

呉氏は、市場改革の一環として、上海証券取引所のハイテク企業向け市場「科創板（スター・マーケット）」と深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」を念頭に、テクノロジー企業の選定の仕組みを改善していくと述べた。中国の資本市場の新商品拡充策の一環として、１８のアクティブ運用型上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）の登録承認についても明らかにした。

世界的な人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の売り圧力を受け、中国の主要指数ＣＳＩ３００指数は、足元では１０週連続で下落している。ハイテク株中心の「科創板」５０指数は６月下旬に付けた今年のピークから４０％近く下落し、年初来の上昇分を失った。

item.title: サウジ、「砂漠のダボス会議」の対面開催中止へ＝関係筋
item.description:
Timour Azhari Federico Maccioni Tala Ramadan Alexander Cornwell
[１９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Timour Azhari　Federico Maccioni　Tala Ramadan　Alexander Cornwell

[１９日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアが主催する国際投資会議「フューチャー・インベストメント・イニシアチブ（ＦＩＩ）」について、同国政府は今年の対面開催を中止することを決めた。関係筋４人が明らかにした。

中東紛争の拡大に伴う一連の攻撃で国内に多数の犠牲者が出て、経済活動が混乱していることを受けた。

ＦＩＩは１０月２６日から２９日の日程で開催される予定だったが、オンライン開催に切り替えるか、延期される見通し。

世界の首脳や大企業の経営者、金融関係者が多数参加することから、ＦＩＩは世界経済フォーラム年次総会になぞらえて「砂漠のダボス会議」と呼ばれている。

サウジ政府の広報室はコメント要請にすぐには応じなかった。

item.title: 米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準 ローン金利・建材高が重し
item.description: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準　ローン金利・建材高が重し 10/19 23:47 配信

米カリフォルニア州エンシニタスにある一戸建て住宅。８月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ住宅建設業者指数は２９と、前月の３２から低下し、２０１２年６月以来、約１４年半ぶりの低水準となった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は３１への低下だった。

中東紛争により住宅ローン金利とエネルギー関連の建材価格が上昇しているほか、移民取り締まりに伴う人手不足や、関税措置によるコスト上昇が影響している。

住宅ローン金利はここ数週間で急上昇しており、住宅金融公社フレディマックのデータによると、３０年固定住宅ローン金利は先週、７．４０％と約３年ぶりの高水準となった。米国とイスラエルの対イラン戦争がインフレをあおる中、米国債利回りに連動して借り入れコストが上昇し、住宅販売を圧迫している。

ＮＡＨＢのビル・オーウェンズ会長は「住宅建設業者は、建設ローンや建築建材、ディーゼル燃料のコスト上昇に加え、慢性的な人手不足にも直面している」と指摘。「全米で建設業者の３分の１超が、過去１カ月間に自社の事業地域で移民取り締まりの動きがあったと報告しており、これが建設の遅れや、合法的な労働者が出勤を躊躇（ちゅうちょ）する事態を招いている」と述べた。

買い手を呼び込むために値下げを実施した建設業者は４３％と、２０─２６年の期間で最も高い割合となった。平均値下げ幅は６％と横ばいだった。販売促進策の実施率は６５％。１９カ月連続で６０％以上となっている。

現在の販売状況を示す指数は２ポイント低下の３３。販売見通しを示す指数は５ポイント低下の３２となった。

見込み客の来場状況を示す指数は５ポイント低下の１８。ＮＡＨＢのチーフエコノミスト、ロバート・ディーツ氏は同指数について、コロナ禍の２０年４月を除くと、１２年４月以来の低水準だと指摘した。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める アングル：ドル高支える年金基金のヘッジ巻き戻し、市場環境変化で懸念後退 アングル：今年はバリュー投資が活発化か、ＡＩバブル懸念で着目点変化 アングル：米株のテック依存、「ＩＴバブル期」上回る　市場を不安定に アングル：米国株、人気は株主還元よりＡＩ技術革新投資の企業 最終更新: 10/19(月) 23:47 ロイター

item.title: ホルムズ不安定化「米に責任」、外国勢力伴わぬ安保必要＝イラン外相
item.description: [１９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１９日 ロイター] - イランのアラグチ外相は１９日、ロシアのラブロフ外相との共同記者会見で、ホルムズ海峡の不安定化と緊張の高まりは米国に責任があるとの認識を示し、地域問題は外交を通じて解決されなければならないと述べた。

アラグチ氏は「外国勢力の駐留を伴わず、地域内部から安全保障を実現するあらゆる取り組みを歓迎する。それが正しい方向性だと考えている」と述べ、地域諸国に対し共同の安全保障体制の構築に向けて取り組むよう呼びかけた。

ロシアのラブロフ外相はアラグチ氏との会談で、ロシアはエネルギー価格の大幅な変動に利益を見いだしていないとし、ロシアは長期的な視点で経済と国家の発展を計画する必要があると述べた。

item.title: US says immigrants from Ukraine, Sudan can keep protected status for now
item.description: Immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan can keep their temporary protected status in the United States for now, the Department of Homeland Security said on Monday, the day protections had been set to expire.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan can keep their temporary protected status in the United States for now, the Department of Homeland Security said on Monday, the day protections had been set to expire. In a statement, a DHS spokesperson said that announcements on Ukrainian and Sudanese TPS holders would "be made at the appropriate time" and that their immigration protections would remain in place. [USN:L6N3RN0SH TEXT:"Temporary protected status"] allows people already in the US to stay in the country and work legally if their home countries are affected by natural disasters, armed conflict or other extraordinary conditions. The temporary respite is the second in as many months for certain immigrants under the TPS program, even as US President Donald Trump has moved to expel other foreign nationals as part of an aggressive immigration crackdown. In September, his administration allowed TPS holders from [USN:L1N45117M TEXT:"El Salvador"] to retain their protections after earlier moving to revoke them from Haitians, Venezuelans, Somalis, Yemenis, Syrians and others. The latest allowance comes as Trump has pivoted away from Ukraine in recent days, [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"declining to impose"] tougher sanctions on Russia over the four-year-old war and lifting sanctions on Moscow's diesel exports. Some [USN:L6N3PN0MX TEXT:"240,000 Ukrainians"] who fled the conflict have registered for TPS status in the United States. There are an estimated 6,800 TPS holders from Sudan, where a war between the army and a rival paramilitary has created one of the world's [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"worst humanitarian crises"]. Global Refuge, a faith-based refugee-focused nonprofit group, welcomed the respite for Ukrainians and Sudanese enrolled in TPS but urged an official decision to give enrollees, their dependents and employers certainty. "The appropriate time to act was weeks ago. Families who depend on this status to stay safe and keep working deserve a formal decision in writing," Krish O'Mara Vignarajah, president and CEO of the group, said in a statement.

item.title: 米国株式市場・午前＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック上昇、ＡＩ関連が反発
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場・午前＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック上昇、ＡＩ関連が反発 10/19 23:33 配信

2026年7月20日に撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が前週の急落から反発したほか、原油価格の下落も支援材料となった。ナスダック総合指数は一時２５５．３ポイント（０．９８％）上昇した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを手がけるコアウィーブは、投資判断の引き上げを受けて３．４％高と急伸した。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、同社の投資判断を「中立」から「買い」に引き上げた。コンピューティング能力の供給が逼迫していることや、競合企業に対する業績面での優位性から、今後２年間でメガワット当たりの年間経常収益が押し上げられるはずだとし、直近の下落は買いの好機だとした。前週には、同社の抱える５００億ドルの債務を巡る懸念がＡＩセクター全体に広がり、株価の４分の１超を失っていた。

競合のネビウス・グループは４．５％高。過去２週間で３１％超下落していた。データセンター運営のアプライド・デジタルは９％、ＩＲＥＮは５．７％、それぞれ上昇した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は２．８％高で推移。前週に１１％超下落し、ＡＩ関連の急落局面で最も打撃を受けた銘柄群の一つとなった。

インテルは５．６％上昇した。ＪＰモルガンが投資判断を「アンダーウエート」から「ニュートラル」に引き上げたことが材料となった。

エヌビディアは０．６％、ＡＭＤは４．３％、ブロードコムは２．２％、それぞれ上昇した。３社とも前週に大きく売られていた。

マイクロン・テクノロジーは３．８％高。前週には約１５％下落していた。データストレージのサンディスク、ウエスタン・デジタル、シーゲイトも前週の大幅安から反発した。

item.title: Ex-OpenAI employee accused of planting device appears to have Saudi backing, US prosecutors say
item.description: An ex-OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company appears to have received considerable support from the Saudi government, US prosecutors said in a court filing.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: An ex-OpenAI engineer accused of [USN:L4N45Z20U TEXT:"planting a recording device"] in an executive conference room at the AI company appears to have received considerable support from the Saudi government, US prosecutors said in a court filing. Federal prosecutors allege that the defendant, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was in frequent communication with an unnamed member of the Saudi royal family and that a Saudi military official paid for a one-way plane ticket for Alfozan's wife and young son to return to Saudi Arabia after his arrest, according to the court document, made public late on Sunday. Prosecutors made those allegations as they asked a federal judge to keep Alfozan in US custody to await trial, arguing he is a flight risk. Alfozan, a Saudi national and lawful permanent resident in the US, is scheduled to appear in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday. The case has highlighted security challenges around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for an edge in the transformational technology. "The defendant went to significant lengths to create customized, encrypted recording devices to secretly record highly sensitive meetings involving senior OpenAI personnel and executives, high-level business counterparts, and government officials, all while communicating with individuals of significance in Saudi Arabia and pursuing opportunities in — and making plans to travel to — Saudi Arabia," prosecutors wrote in a detention memo. The Saudi government media office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A lawyer for Alfozan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawyer, William Pernik, previously asked for Alfozan to be released from custody, subject to conditions including location monitoring and surrendering his passport, and said Alfozan had spent the last 15 years in the US and had applied to become a citizen. The lawyer said a planned trip by Alfozan to Saudi Arabia this month was booked before he was under investigation and was for "family and immigration reasons," according to a court filing. DEVICE INSTALLED BEHIND TV US prosecutors charged Alfozan last week with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications. Alfozan plugged a recording device into the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of OpenAI's San Francisco buildings, according to a criminal complaint. Meetings involving government officials took place in the conference room around the time the device was installed, according to the prosecutors' detention memo. Prosecutors said the investigation remains active and additional charges could be brought against Alfozan. A member of the Saudi royal family sought to recruit Alfozan for an AI-focused role in Saudi Arabia, writing in one message, “Saudi needs you more then the US!" Alfozan replied "100," according to messages cited by prosecutors. Before his arrest, Alfozan was scheduled to fly to Riyadh during a planned two-month parental leave. His wife told investigators that she and their son planned to move permanently to Saudi Arabia and that Alfozan eventually intended to join them, according to prosecutors. In an Arabic-language interview on the Identity Capital podcast last month, Alfozan said that he visits Saudi Arabia three or four times a year, follows developments there and advises or mentors Saudi startups. He said meeting Prince Mohammed bin Salman, then deputy crown prince, during a 2016 gathering with young Saudi tech workers in Silicon Valley persuaded him to learn at a top tech company before bringing those skills back home. While Alfozan was working at Facebook, he and other Saudis in Silicon Valley formed a consulting initiative that linked Saudi public- and private-sector organizations with expertise in big data, the internet of things and machine learning. OpenAI previously said it discovered the device on September 30 and referred the matter to the FBI.

item.title: 米、中国ディープシークを民生部門ＩＴから排除 情報流出懸念
item.description: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　１９日　ロイター] - 米国土安全保障省（ＤＨＳ）は、米政府の民生部門のＩＴシステムから、中国の新興人工知能（ＡＩ）企業ディープシークの製品および同社製モデルを使用した第三者サービスの排除を命じている。１９日に公表された通知から明らかになった。

同省はまた、米政府の民生部門によるディープシーク製品およびディープシークを用いて開発された第三者サービスの調達も禁止する。同省は、ディープシークのモデルは「複数の脅威の経路」をもたらすと指摘。米政府職員や取引業者が使用した場合、「機密データが中国に流出する可能性がある」との懸念を示した。

さらに、政府機関によるディープシークの利用は「米国民や政府機関に関し、具体的な工作につながる機密情報を生み出す可能性がある。モデル自体にマルウエアやその他のセキュリティー上の脆弱性が含まれている恐れがある」と指摘した。

ＤＨＳは１９日に公表された７月付のメモで、ディープシークに関する潜在的なリスクに対処するため、政府ウェブサイトを出入りするトラフィックの流れを監視するよう連邦機関に指示した。

これまでに米商務省や海軍を含む複数の機関が、政府支給の端末でのディープシークの使用を禁止しているほか、ニューヨーク、テネシー、バージニア各州など複数の州も同様の措置を講じている。

在ワシントンの中国大使館はコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 19 : Nvidia has won central processor chip business with another fast-growing AI startup that until now relied entirely on chips from Intel and AMD, an early sign that its push into a market long controlled by those two rivals has traction. Modal, a cloud-computing startup that rents out computing power to AI developers, said it plans to start using Nvidia's new Vera central processor for the first time for hosting agents, the AI systems that can carry out long-running tasks for human users. Modal until now has run such work only on Intel and AMD chips. Modal last week raised $750 million in a funding round led by Accel at a $15.75 billion valuation, saying it is on track to record $1 billion in sales over the next year. Modal said usage of its services has tripled and revenue has grown more than 15 times year-over-year. Modal said Monday that early tests showed the new Nvidia chip doubled the amount of work that AI agents can get done, prompting the company to support Nvidia's chip design for the first time, which will require some deep software changes on Modal's side.

But Chief Executive Erik Bernhardsson was careful to stress it is not abandoning its existing suppliers. The company said it will run the Nvidia chips alongside its current Intel and AMD offerings in a mixed fleet, putting each job on whatever hardware runs it best. Bernhardsson said the tests were run against the Intel and AMD chips already on the market. Both Nvidia rivals are developing newer models that could narrow the gap with Nvidia. "We'll test them when they're available," he said, adding that running a mixed setup means the company "can always deploy whatever hardware performs best." Nvidia has told investors it expects to generate at least $20 billion from Vera chip sales this fiscal year, its opening bid for a market it values at roughly $200 billion. Nvidia has previously said OpenAI, Anthropic and Oracle also plan to use the chips, along with AI startups such as Perplexity.

item.title: Hungary to cut deficit below 5% of GDP in Magyar's first budget plan
item.description: Hungary's budget will target a much lower deficit of 4.9% of gross domestic product in 2027, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Monday as he unveiled the government's draft plan, seen as a credibility test for its ambitions to adopt the euro.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Szakacs, Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: Hungary's budget will target a much lower deficit of 4.9% of gross domestic product in 2027, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Monday as he unveiled the government's draft plan, seen as a credibility test for its ambitions to adopt the euro. Magyar's government inherited an estimated 7.5% of GDP budget shortfall from former prime minister Viktor Orban this year, and its plan is more ambitious than a 5.3% deficit expected by analysts in a Reuters poll last week. "We need only look around Europe to understand the scale of its significance and what is at stake," Magyar told parliament in a speech presenting the 2027 budget that lasted more than two hours. "The examples of France or Romania show exactly where it leads when a government is unable to curb overspending, corruption and theft for years," he said. The budget will include a 300 billion forint (826 million euro) contingency reserve. The announcement of the deficit target sent the forint , central Europe's best-performing currency this year, to four-week highs versus the euro. Magyar and his government are aiming to narrow the deficit to below the EU's 3% target ceiling by 2030 while still honouring their pledges to voters that helped secure his landslide election win over Orban in April. Magyar said he would use billions of euros of European Union funds released after the rollback of Orban-era reforms seen as harming democracy to launch large-scale investments in housing, infrastructure and water management to mitigate climate change. "The 4.9% deficit target appears somewhat better than market expectations going into the announcement, although the key question now is delivery," said Yvette Babb, a fund manager at William Blair. MAGYAR ADDS MORE THAN $6.2 BILLION OF NEW SPENDING New spending is set to reach more than 2 trillion forints ($6.2 billion) next year, including 449 billion in pension increases, 677 billion in public sector wage hikes, a doubling of the family allowance and tax cuts for more than 2 million people on lower incomes. Magyar said the phase-out of Orban's pre-election largesse and one-off spending would improve the budget balance by 1.4 percentage points. A wealth tax and tax rises on large companies would add 1 percentage point of revenue, he said. Cutting back on corruption and public sector overspending would save 1.5 percentage points of output, with lower debt-servicing costs trimming another 0.1 to 0.2 point, he said, bringing the overall fiscal balance improvement to 4 percentage points. Magyar said he would use 1.4 percentage points of that leeway to deliver on election promises, while the remaining 2.6 points would be used to curb the deficit. The government will launch a 200 billion forint wealth tax, increase taxes on energy companies by 100 billion forints and raise the corporate tax by 2 percentage points to 11% for companies with annual turnover over €500 million. Spending to ease the burden of energy price spikes on households, a costly Orban-era measure, which the EU has called on Hungary to eliminate, will remain in place. The government's aim to adopt the euro has triggered a rally in Hungary's forint , which helped drive inflation below the central bank's target, while bond yields have tumbled this year and are among the lowest in central Europe. Analysts see Hungary joining the euro in 2032 or 2033. (1 euro = 363.0084 forints)

item.title: 仏北部4都市に夜間外出禁止令、首相が極左勢力の暴動関与を非難
item.description: [パリ １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[パリ １９日 ロイター] - フランス当局は１９日、北部リールに１９日１８００ＧＭＴ（日本時間２０日午前３時）から２０日０４００ＧＭＴ（同午後１時）までの夜間外出禁止令を出した。首相府関係者が明らかにした。同関係者によると、夜間外出禁止令は２日間にわたり実施され、北部のドゥエー、ワティニー、ドゥナンも対象となる。

週末に全国で暴動が発生したことを受けた措置。

ルコルニュ首相は、一部地域で夜間外出禁止令を出すよう地方当局に要請していた。首相は、パリ全域を対象とする全面的な夜間外出禁止令は否定したが、非常事態宣言については排除しなかった。ただ、現段階では部分的かつ地域限定の夜間外出禁止令の方がより適切との考えを示し、詳細には触れなかった。

また、今回の騒乱の一部について極左グループの関与を非難。「大統領選を前に、国内に深刻な混乱を引き起こそうとする極左の動きが確かに存在する。これ以上強い言い方はできない」と述べた。

これに対し、極左政党「不屈のフランス（ＬＦＩ）」を率いるジャンリュック・メランション氏は強く反発。ルコルニュ首相に対し証拠を示すよう求め、「さもなくば謝罪し、沈黙し、騒乱の火に油を注ぐのをやめるべきだ」とＸに投稿した。

フランス大統領選の世論調査では、メランション氏と極右政党「国民連合（ＲＮ）」の実質的な指導者マリーヌ・ルペン氏が他の候補者に対するリードを広げ、決選投票で一騎打ちになるとの見通しが示されている。

週末の暴動や略奪の爪痕が残る中、フランスの主要都市の市長らは１９日、治安部隊の準備が不足していたとして政府に説明を求めた。

１７日には、生活費の高騰と公共サービスの質の低下に抗議するデモが一部で暴徒化し、同国で過去数十年で最大規模の暴動に発展した。

商業・小売連盟によると、週末に被害を受けた店舗は約３０００店に上っている。

Erlangen, GERMANY, Oct 19 : AI could help preserve manufacturing jobs in high-wage countries such as Germany by boosting factory automation to as much as 80 per cent, Siemens executive board member Cedrik Neike said on Monday. Speaking at the company's electronics plant in Erlangen, Neike said manufacturers need annual productivity gains of 7 per cent-9 per cent to remain competitive. • Siemens aims to harness AI to raise the level of automation in factory manufacturing to 70 per cent-80 per cent from 30 per cent-40 per cent currently, Neike said. • Siemens and Nvidia are working on the use of "physical AI" in manufacturing, using digital twins and AI models to simulate and optimise factory operations before they are deployed on the factory floor.

item.title: 米ロ中首脳、ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議に合わせ会談の可能性＝ロシア大統領報道官
item.description: [モスクワ １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ　１９日　ロイター] - ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は１９日、プーチン大統領、トランプ米大統領、中国の習近平国家主席が来月中国で開催されるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせて３者会談を行う可能性があるとの見方を示し、そうした会談について協議で言及されたと明らかにした。

ペスコフ大統領報道官は、ロシアとウクライナの戦闘終結に向けた協議を行うため、プーチン氏が米ロ中の首脳会談を提案したとする米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）の報道について質問され、「３首脳全員が中国で開かれる首脳会議に参加する可能性があることを踏まえ、そうした会談の可能性が実際に話題に上った」とした上で、「実際に議題に上ったが、会談そのものや会談の議題、内容について具体的な提案や合意が協議されたり、提示されたりしていない」と述べた。

また、米国はロシアとウクライナの戦闘終結に向けた仲介努力を続けており、ロシアはその取り組みを評価していると指摘。最終的な和平合意にはウクライナの参加が不可欠との認識を示した。

米ロ中首脳会談の可能性についてルビオ米国務長官は１９日、訪問先のウズベキスタンで記者団に対し「会談の話は出ている。最終決定したかどうかは分からないが、トランプ大統領の意向は明確だ。大統領はウクライナとロシア間の戦争が終わることを望んでいる」と述べている。

ウクライナのシビハ外相は、米ロ中の首脳による会談の構想を非難。「ウクライナ、米国、ロシアの首脳による３者会談なら、戦争終結の早期実現の一助になり得る。ロシア、中国、米国の首脳による３者会談はその逆の効果しかなく、プーチン氏が戦争を継続することを後押しするだけだ」とＸに投稿した。

item.title: イエメン暫定政府の訓練施設攻撃で53人死亡、フーシ派が犯行声明
item.description: [１９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１９日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１９日、同国中南部シャブワ州にある暫定政府治安部隊の訓練施設を攻撃し、５３人が死亡、２００人が負傷した。地元当局が明らかにした。貧困にあえぐ同国での戦闘が激化している。

フーシ派のヤヒヤ・サリー報道官はＸへの投稿で、同派が訓練施設を標的にしたと表明。同施設はサウジアラビア軍が運営していたと主張した。サウジ当局はコメント要請に即座には応じなかった。

匿名を条件に取材に応じた地元当局筋によると、フーシ派は訓練中の治安部隊に向け、弾道ミサイル３発を発射した。シャブワ州はイエメン中南部沿岸に位置するエネルギー資源が豊富な州で、同国最大の産業投資であるバルハフ液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）施設がある。

イエメン暫定政府軍は今月、フーシ派が支配する地域の奪還を目指す作戦を開始し、バベルマンデブ海峡付近の領土を取り戻した。一方、フーシ派は、イエメン南部山岳地帯における反フーシ派勢力の最後の主要都市拠点であるタイズを包囲している。

WASHINGTON, Oct 19 : Meta apologized for suspending the Instagram account of the "No Kings" protest movement over the weekend, attributing the shutdown to a sharp increase in activity that looked like automated bot traffic rather than human exchanges. Demonstrators gathered at thousands of events across the United States on Saturday decrying President Donald Trump's aggressive deportation efforts, war in Iran and other policies in the third round of the "No Kings" rallies. The Instagram account used by organizers and attendees, however, was offline for more than an hour. And Meta spokesman Andy Stone wrote in a post on X that it took longer to fix problems with organizers' access to the accounts.  Stone said network security systems detected the use of a Claude tool reading profiles, posts, and hashtags, with the rate sharply increasing in intense bursts on October 17.

"These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems. This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline," he said. "We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error." Rally organizers were not satisfied on Monday. "Meta's explanation still doesn't add up," the No Kings Coalition said on the Bluesky platform. "Beyond shutting down our Instagram, we’ve received reports that NoKings and early voting content was inaccessible, restricted, or seemed suppressed across Meta platforms."  "Weeks before an election, an apology isn't enough. The public needs answers, accountability, and concrete safeguards," the coalition said. "No Kings" rallies took place in cities from Seattle and San Diego to Chicago, Atlanta and New York. In Washington, DC, protesters gathered at the site of Trump's proposed triumphal arch to encourage early voting before the November 3 midterm congressional elections.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 19 : The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a challenge by Alphabet's Google to a US Patent and Trademark Office rule that the company argued has insulated older patents from validity reviews and helped fuel a surge in patent litigation. The justices turned away Google's appeal of a lower court's decision not to force the agency to reconsider, without using its "settled expectations" rule, the company's challenge to the validity of a patent held by software company VirtaMove. VirtaMove accused Google of infringing the patent. Google asked the Supreme Court to review the "settled expectations" policy, under which the patent office's Patent Trial and Appeal Board, or PTAB, became more likely to reject requests to review patents that have been in force for more than six years. Technology companies often use the board's "inter partes review" process to try to cancel patents that they are accused of infringing. The three most active board petitioners between 2020 and 2025 were Samsung, Apple and Alphabet, according to a report from IP company Patexia.

The USPTO during President Donald Trump's administration has introduced measures that have decreased the percentage of reviews the board takes up.  That figure fell to 37 per cent in 2026 under John Squires, the Trump appointee who heads the patent office, compared to 65 per cent under his predecessor Kathi Vidal, who was appointed by former President Joe Biden, according to an April report from the agency. The patent office outlined in a memo last year several factors that favor rejecting an inter partes review petition, which the agency has used to deny review for patents that are more than six years old based on the "settled expectations" of the parties. The patent office cited the "settled expectations" rule in rejecting Google's review petition in 2025 concerning the VirtaMove patent involving server software. The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit ruled against Google's appeal of the patent office rejection. Google told the justices in a filing that the rule exceeds the patent office's authority by creating an artificial time limit for board petitions. "The PTO (Patent and Trademark Office) has no authority to create a limitations period where Congress did not, and it has no authority to expand patent rights beyond what Congress provided," Google said in the filing. The Trump administration urged the court not to hear Google's appeal. A group of companies including Google, Apple and Intel has filed a separate lawsuit challenging a related patent office policy. The Federal Circuit ruled against the companies in February, and Intel and Google have also asked the Supreme Court to hear that case.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Oct 19 : A decision on Senegal's appeal after being stripped of this year's Africa Cup of Nations title will be made at the end of November, the Court of Arbitration for Sport said on Monday. Senegal are contesting the Confederation of African Football's decision to declare Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in January's final in Rabat, and their arguments, plus those of Morocco and CAF, were heard by CAS in Lausanne on October 8. At the time, CAS said it expected a decision within days but has now decided to issue a complete ruling, including legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. “This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026,” CAS said in a statement.

Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty was awarded against them late in regulation time, with several players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play. Morocco missed the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal scored the winner to secure victory. However, they were stripped of the title two months later after CAF's Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco.  Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court CAS, which was lodged on March 25 but heard some six months later. The basis of their arguments is that the referee’s decision is final and he allowed the match to be completed.  "I know it's a long wait for the fans a few months after the final between Senegal and Morocco,” CAS Director General Matthieu Reeb said outside the hearing earlier this month. “I expect the decision to come not today, not tomorrow, but a few days later. The facts are set, are clear and the discussions will be on some procedural issues and legal aspects," he added. The CAS panel is presided over by French sports law expert Gerald Simon with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of law at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas. CAS decisions are called awards and hold the same value as a national court judgement, enforceable in accordance with the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards. CAS awards may be enforced by sports federations or state courts, depending on the circumstances.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson; Editing by Ken Ferris)

Source: Reuters

item.title: US Supreme Court to hear Maryland case involving race in school admissions
item.description: The US Supreme Court agreed on Monday to consider reviving a lawsuit against a Maryland county's lottery admissions policy for four elite public middle schools that some parents claim unlawfully discriminates against Asian American applicants.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court agreed on Monday to consider reviving a lawsuit against a Maryland county's lottery admissions policy for four elite public middle schools that some parents claim unlawfully discriminates against Asian American applicants. Delving again into the contentious issue of race in student admissions, the justices took up an appeal by a coalition of parents of a lower court's decision rejecting their claim that Montgomery County's policy violates the US Constitution's 14th Amendment guarantee of equal protection under the law. The Supreme Court is expected to hear the case and rule by the end of June. The parents sued to challenge the entrance policies for the county's academically rigorous "magnet" schools, which provide enrichment programs in math and science, or the humanities, for high-achieving students in sixth through eighth grades. They include Takoma Park Middle School in Silver Spring and Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School in Germantown. The case represents the latest legal attack on entrance policies at certain highly selective public schools that challengers critique for continuing to pursue "racial balancing" with the aim of boosting diversity. The Supreme Court issued a landmark 2023 [USN:S0N31105H TEXT:"ruling"] that rejected [USN:L1N38L2JO TEXT:"race-conscious"] college and university admissions policies long used to raise the number of Black, Hispanic and other minority students on campuses. Plaintiffs in these new legal challenges claim that admissions to these prestigious programs, though race-neutral on the surface, use proxies such as socioeconomic status to achieve the same unlawful, race-based result in pursuit of diversity. The legal challenges coincide with President Donald Trump 's policies, implemented since he returned to office last year, against diversity, equity and inclusion, or DEI, programs in education, as well as in the US government and military, and in private companies. At issue in the Maryland case is whether lower courts may dismiss claims of intentional racial discrimination if the policy has not disproportionately harmed that racial group, in this instance Asian American students. Montgomery County is a wealthy suburb of Washington, DC. The parent coalition, called the Association for Education Fairness, is represented by the Pacific Legal Foundation, a libertarian legal group that has pursued similar challenges in Virginia and Massachusetts. The Supreme Court [USN:S0N3AA01J TEXT:"rejected"] those [USN:S0N3IS01A TEXT:"cases"] in 2024. "The Constitution protects students as individuals, not as members of a racial group," said Chris Kieser, an attorney for the coalition. "A school district should not be able to defeat a discrimination claim by showing that its policy did not harm enough Asian American children. Every family deserves admissions rules that judge their child on their own merit," Kieser said. ENRICHED INSTRUCTION The Montgomery County school district's selection process was introduced in the 2021-2022 school year, during the COVID-19 pandemic. It screens all students for academic potential, and then implements a lottery to randomly assign students from that pool to receive enriched instruction at either a magnet school or a local school. The lawsuit said that the lottery system led to a lower number of Asian American student placements at the magnet schools. The suit alleged that the screening process makes it harder for Asian American students, who the challengers said are clustered in "high-performing, low-poverty elementary schools," to enter the lottery pool. Part of the process ranks a student's performance by comparing the student's test scores against those of other students whose family incomes are at a similar level. US District Judge Paula Xinis threw out the case in 2022, finding that the policy did not place a disproportionate burden on Asian American students. The judge noted that the percentage of admitted Asian American students exceeded the percentage of Asian Americans among all applicants to the magnet schools. Xinis also found that there was no evidence that the lottery policy was implemented with discriminatory intent. The Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the dismissal, agreeing that the lawsuit "does not plausibly allege that the challenged policy disparately impacts Asian American students." The Supreme Court's 2023 affirmative action ruling upended decades of precedent, striking down programs used by Harvard University and the University of North Carolina that took race into account as one of many factors in student admissions evaluations.

LONDON, Oct 19 : Britain risks becoming a "high-value AI customer" rather than a country able to shape the technology unless it takes urgent action to build domestic capabilities, the government's top science advisers said on Monday. Governments around the world are racing to build AI capabilities, driven by concerns that countries without their own expertise, computing infrastructure and models could become increasingly dependent on a handful of mostly U.S.-based companies that dominate the technology. The Council for Science and Technology, an independent advisory body that advises the government on science and technology policy, said decisions made now would determine whether Britain captures the economic and public benefits of AI while maintaining resilience and strategic autonomy. "The way for us to achieve AI sovereignty is to build trusted systems that deliver real public, economic and security benefits," the advisers said in an emailed letter to the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan.

The council warned that Britain was at risk of falling behind and becoming a "high-value AI customer, rather than a country able to shape the technology and its usage," without what it described as "deliberate and urgent action." It recommended appointing a single government lead to coordinate AI sovereignty policy, investing in skills, data and computing infrastructure, and testing AI systems in areas including national security, health and education. The advisers also said Britain should maintain access to the world's most advanced AI systems while developing some domestic capabilities of its own, including exploring a publicly governed British AI model that could be made available to researchers, startups and public services. The government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months
item.description: France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into turmoil, exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order.
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"turmoil"], exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order. The [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"rioting"] that swept across France on Saturday, leaving a trail of looted shops, torched buildings and defaced public institutions, presents Macron with perhaps the most explosive challenge of his twilight presidency: a country demanding more from a state that can no longer afford to give much. Macron came to power almost a decade ago promising to upend France’s sclerotic political class, turbocharge economic reforms and restore authority through a more assertive presidency. Instead, with just six months left in office, he finds himself effectively a lame-duck head of state presiding over a country mired in political paralysis, facing acute [USN:L6N46502R TEXT:"financial pressures"] and grappling with unrest that has exposed the limits of state authority. Unlike during the Yellow Vest uprising of 2018-2019, when Macron sought to defuse public anger with billions of euros in concessions, France’s strained public finances and fractured parliament leave him with precious few levers to pull. Even former allies are now openly scathing, tracing the country's current impasse to Macron's decision to call a [USN:L8N3J00J1 TEXT:"snap parliamentary election"] in 2024 that weakened his authority. “The end of this term is a slow agony,” said Loïc Kervran, a former lawmaker from Macron’s camp, on X. “The president paralysed the country with his absurd decision to dissolve parliament in 2024. Arguably the worst decision in the history of the Fifth Republic." LE PEN'S 'HIGHWAY' TO THE PRESIDENCY The turmoil may benefit far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race and stands to gain from both the anger over declining living standards and the fears over law and order unleashed by the weekend’s violence. "Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, another former Macron lawmaker, told Reuters. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her — it's a six-lane highway." Le Pen delivered her own message to the nation in a video statement on Sunday, portraying Macron's administration as a crumbling power and casting herself as the figure capable of restoring order. When Macron later addressed the country, he offered little concrete action, stopping short of declaring a state of emergency. As he spoke, looting was continuing for a second consecutive night, including in affluent Paris districts, prompting his prime minister Sébastien Lecornu to announce local curfews on Monday. Opponents and one-time allies alike were underwhelmed. His former prime minister, Edouard Philippe, now preparing his own presidential run, was unsparing in his criticism. "Mr President, I listened to you last night," he wrote on X. "I would have preferred, like millions of French people, decisions and initiatives to restore order." "Our country needs to be commanded," he added. But even Philippe is struggling to shake off his past association with Macron, and most recent polls show far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon edging ahead of him in the race to qualify for the second-round runoff vote. That outcome would all but guarantee a Le Pen victory, according to opinion polls. CALLS FOR EARLY RESIGNATION AMID MULTIPLE CRISES Macron's office on Monday announced that he had refused his interior minister's resignation and ordered a review into apparent failures in intelligence gathering and police preparedness — deepening the impression of a government struggling to regain control. [USN:L1N465097 TEXT:"Investors also took fright"]. Market analysts say the violence adds another layer of political risk at a time when France is already under scrutiny over its swelling debt burden and struggle to reduce one of the euro zone's largest budget deficits. The president now finds himself trapped between bond markets demanding spending restraint and protesters demanding the opposite. Despite calls from opponents to remain in France, Macron arrived in Kuwait on Monday on a Gulf tour he says will help secure fuel supplies and ease some of the economic pressures that have helped swell the ranks of the protesters. The trip carries risks, reinforcing perceptions of a president disconnected from the public mood. Images of Macron attending a Céline Dion concert with his wife Brigitte on Friday evening, hours before the unrest erupted, prompted ridicule on social media and became an easy symbol for critics seeking to portray him as detached from events. In a sign of the depth of disenchantment in parts of his political camp, some former allies have begun openly discussing whether he should leave office before the end of his term. Moreau, who spoke to Macron on Sunday, said he urged him to prepare an orderly early departure to break the current political deadlock and avoid another six months of drift. "He doesn't want to give up, that's not his character. But that's what he should do for the country," he said.

item.title: Suède-La dirigeante du Parti du Centre va étudier la possibilité de former un gouvernement
item.description: Le président du Parlement suédois a déclaré lundi avoir demandé à la dirigeante du Parti du Centre, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, d'étudier les possibilités de formation d'un nouveau gouvernement, lui accordant une semaine pour rencontrer les autres partis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président du Parlement suédois a déclaré lundi avoir demandé à la dirigeante du Parti du Centre, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, d'étudier les possibilités de formation d'un nouveau gouvernement, lui accordant une semaine pour rencontrer les autres partis. [USN:L8N45600R TEXT:"Les élections du mois dernier"] ont donné au centre-gauche une courte majorité au Parlement, mais si les quatre partis le constituant, dont le Parti du Centre, soutiennent l'accession de la cheffe de file des sociaux-démocrates, Magdalena Andersson, au poste de Première ministre, ils ne s'accordent pas sur la composition du nouveau gouvernement. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist va désormais étudier une alternative centriste, a déclaré le président du Riksdag, Andreas Norlen, lors d'une conférence de presse, ajoutant qu’il n’était pas certain de savoir qui deviendrait Premier ministre en cas de succès des discussions. "Différentes options gouvernementales sont également à l’étude, mais aucune ne semble progresser clairement, pour autant que je puisse en juger", a déclaré Andreas Norlen. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, dont le parti est arrivé en cinquième position lors des élections du mois dernier, a déclaré qu'elle inviterait tous les chefs de parti à des discussions. "Mon ambition est de contribuer à trouver une solution à la question de la formation du gouvernement et non de devenir moi-même Première ministre", a-t-elle ajouté dans un message publié sur la plate-forme X. [USN:L8N45K0DO TEXT:"Les députés"] ont rejeté jeudi, comme largement attendu, la proposition de Magdalena Andersson de former un gouvernement minoritaire, lors du premier des quatre votes au maximum avant la convocation obligatoire de nouvelles élections. La Suède n’a pas organisé d'élections anticipées depuis 1958.

item.title: ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求 市場改革も表明
item.description:
Ankur Banerjee Stefanno Sulaiman
[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求　市場改革も表明 10/19 22:13 配信

株価ボード、ジャカルタのインドネシア証券取引所で16日撮影 REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/File Photo

Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア株式市場は１９日、２営業日の下落としては過去最大を記録した。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが１６日、２０２７年に同国を「新興国市場」から除外する可能性を警告したことが売りを誘発。当局はＭＳＣＩに説明を求めた。

ジャカルタ総合指数は１６日に１１．６％急落したのに続き、１９日は３．６％安で取引を終えた。２営業日の下落率は１９９８年のアジア金融危機時を含め過去最大となった。取引時間中には６年ぶりの安値も付けた。

ＭＳＣＩが１６日、インドネシアを「新興国市場」から「スタンドアローン市場」に変更することを検討していると表明したことで売りが始まった。想定以上に厳しい分類変更の可能性に、投資家や当局者に動揺が広がった。

スタンドアローン市場に変更されれば、東南アジア最大の経済規模を持つインドネシアは国際資本へのアクセスを失い、投資先として周縁に追いやられる恐れがある。

不安心理からの売りは通貨や債券市場にも波及した。ルピアは１ドル＝１万８０３０ルピアに下落、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに迫った。国債も下落し、１０年債利回りは１６日の７．１６９％から７．４％に上昇した。

インドネシア証券取引所のジェフリー・ヘンドリック最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、説明を求めるためのＭＳＣＩとの会合を前に「（ＭＳＣＩから）このような発表があるとは予想していなかった。予想外の声明で市場はパニックに陥った」と述べた。

＜資本市場改革への取り組み継続＞

ヘンドリック氏はＭＳＣＩとのオンライン会合後、１月にＭＳＣＩが最初の警告を発したことを受けて着手した資本市場改革に引き続き取り組むと述べた。会合の詳細は明らかにできないとした。

同氏はまた、市場の透明性と価格発見機能を改善するための２つの施策を発表した。同一の個人や法人に株式保有が高度に集中している銘柄をジャカルタ総合指数から除外する措置が含まれる。「主要指数の動きをより正確に示す」ことが狙いという。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、価格変動の抑制に向け、株価の１日の下落率の上限を１５％から７％に縮小した。それを下回る価格での売り注文を自動的に拒否し、一段の下落を防ぐ。

＜投資家、インドネシア資産への投資を再評価＞

ＭＳＣＩの動きを受け、投資家がインドネシア資産全般への投資を見直す中、規制当局や財政・金融当局への圧力が強まっている。

かつて新興国市場の有望な投資先だった同国からの資本逃避リスクへの懸念も高まった。投資家によると、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック以降、プラボウォ大統領の下で財政の健全性や中央銀行の独立性への信頼が薄れる中、同国の魅力は既に低下していた。

事情に詳しい政府当局者２人によると、プラボウォ氏は１９日、財政・金融当局者と会合を開き、「現在の経済情勢」について協議した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・レーティングのソブリン担当アナリスト、レイン・リン氏は、ＭＳＣＩの最新の警告で追加の資本流出が起きる可能性が高いものの、資金調達コストを大幅に押し上げる規模にはならないとの見方を示した。「より懸念されるのは、投資家の信頼が損なわれる可能性と、国債市場や海外直接投資にも投資家心理の悪化が広く波及するリスクだ」と述べた。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩ指数から完全に除外されれば、パッシブ運用資金が５６億ドル流出する可能性があると推計。これらの指数をベンチマークとするアクティブ運用ファンドの保有額は８０億ドルを超えるものの、売却するかどうかは指数への連動ではなく、運用者の裁量によると記した。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株を４９億８０００万ドル売り越している。年間の資金流出額は少なくとも過去１６年で最大となるペースだ。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：北朝鮮が韓国と対立姿勢、米国にとって新たな悩みの種に 焦点：新興国投資ラッシュに取り残されるインドネシア、強い政策への不信感 アングル：スマトラ島豪雨被害、森林破壊で被害拡大か　地元に怒りの声 アングル：石炭依存の東南アジア、長期電力購入契約がエネ移行の妨げに 最終更新: 10/19(月) 22:13 ロイター

item.title: Woman tells UK court that comedian Russell Brand raped her
item.description: A woman told police that British actor and comedian Russell Brand had grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet at a bar and orally raping her, a London court heard on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden
item.content:encoded: A woman told police that British actor and comedian [USN:L8N4600OQ TEXT:"Russell Brand"] had grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet at a bar and orally raping her, a London court heard on Monday. Brand, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and the former husband of US singer Katy Perry, is [USN:L1N4610E0 TEXT:"on trial accused"] of three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women between 1999 and 2009. The 51-year-old denies the allegations, and told police after his arrest that he had never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity and the accusers might have re-imagined events. The third of the six complainants to give evidence alleged Brand had assaulted her after she met him at a party in a London bar in 2004. BRAND HAD A WEIRD GRIN, WOMAN SAYS In a tearful police interview played to jurors at Southwark Crown Court, the woman, who worked for MTV, said she had wanted to meet Brand because she had seen him on television and thought he was really funny. But less than a minute after talking to him at the bar, she said, he assaulted her. "He literally just grabbed my boobs in the middle of the conversation," she said, adding that he had a weird, maniacal grin on his face as he did it. Immediately afterwards while she was in shock and disbelief, she said he grabbed her arm and pulled her to the toilets that were nearby. It was there that he allegedly orally raped her. "It happened so fast," she told police. "He said 'come on, come on, don't be a spoilsport'," she recounted, saying he was holding her forcibly by her head and hair. "I just froze. I didn't know what to do." She said while his words were not threatening, the force of the encounter and the look in his eye had been. She rejected Brand's lawyer Ian Winter's suggestion that she had been very excited to meet him, saying she "wasn't star struck ... I wasn't a giddy schoolgirl". Winter put it to her that had she been groped at the bar or dragged into the toilets, people would have seen. "Let's be clear he did not do that to you," he said of the alleged sexual assault. "You happily accompanied Mr Brand into the lavatory," he added, a suggestion she rejected. He said the alleged incident in the toilet was "physically impossible and it did not happen". Winter also queried why she had never said she was raped until after a 2023 documentary and press report about Brand, having told friends and her sister he had tried to force himself on her but she had got away. "I didn't want people to judge me ... I felt ashamed," she said. Last week, the first complainant told the court that Brand had raped her after she met him at a fringe event at the 1999 Labour Party conference in southern England. The second of the complainants told London's Southwark Crown Court that in 2001 a "wild-eyed" Brand [USN:L8N46211H TEXT:"had tried to pull her"] into the male toilets at MTV Europe, in London, where she was working. The trial, which is expected to last around six weeks, continues.

item.title: Google, McKinsey strike Brazil carbon removal deal with silvopasture project
item.description: Google and McKinsey have agreed to buy 320,000 metric tons of carbon removal credits over 10 years in its first-ever silvopasture project, as part of its commitments through the Symbiosis Coalition, in what is an emerging approach to climate mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Araujo
item.content:encoded: Google and McKinsey have agreed to buy 320,000 metric tons of carbon removal credits over 10 years in its first-ever silvopasture project, as part of its commitments through the Symbiosis Coalition, in what is an emerging approach to climate mitigation. The long-term purchase agreements announced on Monday will support an effort by Working Trees, a climate technology company, to convert degraded cattle pasture into mixed-species systems across Brazil's southeastern [USN:L1N4620RV TEXT:"Amazon and Cerrado"] regions, the coalition said. Silvopasture integrates trees into cattle pastures, allowing ranching to continue while boosting carbon sequestration and reducing pressure for deforestation. The deal will help fund the restoration of 8,700 hectares (21,500 acres) of degraded and semi-degraded pastureland as part of a broader 50,000-hectare project and is one of the first attempts to deploy carbon-funded silvopasture at a larger scale. "Silvopasture, within the various different approaches for sequestering carbon via natural systems, is one of the pathways with the most promising potential for scale. And carbon finance has a role to play in financing that solution," Julia Strong, executive director of the Symbiosis Coalition, told Reuters. The coalition, whose members include Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google, Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and [USN:L1N45B037 TEXT:"Salesforce"] (CRM.N) , focuses on long-term carbon offset contracts, with pledges for more than 20 million tons of offsets by 2030. Working Trees plants rows of commercial timber and native tree species directly into existing cattle pasture, leaving space for grazing. The company says the model improves cattle productivity while generating future timber revenue that encourages landowners to maintain the systems after carbon-credit income declines. "This project and the potential to scale to millions of hectares in this part of Brazil is a really exciting opportunity to showcase what good looks like," Strong said, adding that Working Trees had demonstrated the model through a pilot project. Working Trees Chief Executive Leif Gonzales-Kramer said the long-term purchase commitments were critical to unlocking investment for such projects. "If you believe that the world will continue to eat beef and that the world will take climate action seriously, the only way that you can actually achieve both at the same time is through silvopasture," he said. Brazil's [USN:L6N45U0TV TEXT:"nascent carbon market"] has attracted increased interest [USN:L1N45B037 TEXT:"from investors and lenders"] as companies seek high-quality carbon-removal projects to meet climate goals. Technology companies, in particular, are looking for ways to [USN:L1N3WI19U TEXT:"offset emissions"] linked to the rapid expansion of energy-intensive artificial intelligence infrastructure. Some critics, however, say the offsets allow polluters to avoid reducing their emissions.

item.title: Myanmar authorities release rare images of Aung San Suu Kyi
item.description: Myanmar's military-backed government on Monday released rare photographs of the country's imprisoned former leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, saying that officials had delivered her books and letters from Britain's King Charles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Myanmar's military-backed government on Monday released rare photographs of the country's imprisoned former leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, saying that officials had delivered her books and letters from Britain's King Charles. The government officials delivered two books — "The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table" and "Soil: The World at Our Feet" — along with a sealed envelope and a diplomatic communication sent by King Charles, according to a social media post from Myanmar's presidential spokesperson Suu Kyi, 81, has been detained since February 2021, when the military ousted her administration and arrested civilian leaders in early-morning raids The delivery shows rare foreign contact with Suu Kyi, whose whereabouts and health have been difficult to determine after the 2021 coup. No foreign leader or envoy has publicly met with her despite requests The Nobel laureate was [USN:L6N41D0F6 TEXT:"moved to house arrest"] in April this year, following an election held under military rule that installed coup leader Min Aung Hlaing as president In August, she [USN:L1N440037 TEXT:"met with a representative"] of the International Committee of the Red Cross following years of questions over her health and wellbeing She is currently serving an [USN:L1N41004U TEXT:"18-year prison sentence"] at a designated residence for a litany of offences — ranging from incitement and corruption to election fraud and violating a state secrets law — all of which she denies

item.title: Amazon says its AI chips will work with popular coding language, challenging Nvidia
item.description: Amazon.com is introducing a new tool that allows its custom AI chips to run code written in the most popular AI coding language without modification, seeking to erode the advantage that underpins Nvidia's dominance in the AI computing market.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Amazon.com (AMZN.O) is introducing a new tool that allows its custom AI chips to run code written in the most popular AI coding language without modification, seeking to erode the advantage that underpins Nvidia's (NVDA.O) dominance in the AI computing market. Shares of the company were up 5% in morning trading, with Morgan Stanley naming Amazon a "top pick". TorchNeuron lets developers run code written in a language called PyTorch on Amazon's Trainium AI chips with a single configuration change and no rewriting needed, according to Amazon's Annapurna Labs chip unit. Amazon, which plans to announce the software at a developer conference in Silicon Valley on Monday, said the software will be publicly released as a free and open-source offering. PyTorch, the open-source framework stewarded by Meta (META.O) , is used by most AI developers. Nvidia has spent more than a decade on its software tool called Cuda that makes PyTorch code run well on Nvidia chips. Other cloud computing players such as Google (GOOGL.O) , which also has its own custom AI chips, are also working to lure away developers from Nvidia [USN:L6N3XL15R TEXT:"with better PyTorch tools"]. Colin Brace, vice president of software for Annapurna Labs, said the move was aimed at reducing the number of steps AI developers must take to try Amazon's in-house chips. "This has been about meeting customers where they're at," he told Reuters in an interview. Brace said more than 30 early customers — spanning robotics, world models and voice AI — are using the new software, and that the switch to Amazon's chips can result in steep cost savings.

FAST

OSLO, Oct 19 : Norway's planned social media ban for children will include provisions targeting "harmful platforms", the government said on Monday, naming messaging and gaming services Roblox, Snapchat and TikTok among those affected. The Nordic country said in April it would present a bill in parliament by the end of the year to ban children from using social media until they turn 16, making technology companies responsible for age verification. It did not name any platforms at the time. Several European nations are seeking to rein in children's social media use after Australia took the lead with the world's first ban on under-16s last December, which included apps such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube. Norway's government said in a statement on Monday that its bill was intended to address the full range of risks children face on social media and that it would affect "many platforms".

"This includes everything from exposure to harmful content and addictive features to illegal marketing and unwanted contact from strangers," Children and Families Minister Lene Vaagslid said in the statement. The planned legislation provides tech companies with an incentive to remove harmful content and addictive features, she said. The ministry went on to define what it called harmful platforms as "social media that, through its design, features or content, poses a risk to children's emotional, cognitive or physical development or safety." "The government believes that platforms such as TikTok, Roblox, and Snapchat will be covered by the law," it said. It did not immediately respond to a question about which other apps could be affected. Snap Inc, Roblox Corporation and TikTok owner ByteDance did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Children and young people will still have access to messaging services and games that are deemed harmless, the ministry said.

item.title: What's behind Egypt's move towards possible military involvement in Saudi-Yemen conflict?
item.description: Egypt's parliament is expected to vote next week on whether to authorise the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis if Riyadh requests its support.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: [USN:L8N46306J TEXT:"Egypt's parliament"] is expected to vote [USN:L6N4650W2 TEXT:"next week"] on whether to authorise the armed forces to help defend [USN:L1N4610OX TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] against attacks by Yemen's Houthis if Riyadh requests its support. The move would bring the Arab world's most populous country closer to direct military involvement in the widening conflicts unleashed by the US-Israeli air assault on Iran in February. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"requested the approval"] in a speech on Saturday, saying Egypt would "never, never forget our brothers in the Gulf" and telling Saudi Arabia's leaders that Cairo would "take any measure to protect you". Like the [USN:L6N4610JI TEXT:"Gulf states"] that have come under attack from Tehran in the Iran war , Egypt is a longstanding partner in the US-led security order that is being tested by the conflict. WHAT IS EGYPT'S STANCE ON THE IRAN WAR? Sisi's comments marked a clear escalation from the more measured tone authorities have tended to adopt since the Iran war started. Though Egypt has repeatedly voiced strong support for its Gulf allies, Cairo has stopped short of publicly committing itself to a direct combat role in the conflict. In May, the presence of Egyptian Rafale fighter jets in the United Arab Emirates was disclosed in Emirati state media coverage of an official visit by Sisi. Egyptian coverage of the visit did not mention the deployment. When Saudi Arabia signed a [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"joint defence agreement"] with Turkey and Pakistan in August, Egypt did not join, though it said it was considering it. The tone started to shift after [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"the Houthis"] stepped up attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman last month visited Egypt, where he discussed the need to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] and the Red Sea, on which both countries have long coastlines. WHAT'S AT STAKE FOR EGYPT? Egypt's economic stability has long been tied up with the oil-producing Gulf. Remittances from Egyptian expatriate workers there are an important source of foreign currency and income for families back home at a time of double-digit inflation worsened by surging food and fuel prices. Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf countries have been among Sisi's key financial backers, providing tens of billions of dollars of aid, central bank deposits and investments since the army overthrew President Mohamed Morsi, a senior Muslim Brotherhood figure, in 2013. "We can never forget how our brothers in the Gulf states stood by Egypt during that period," Sisi said in his speech. Saudi Arabia has a $5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month along with $267 million in interest, central bank data shows. WHAT ABOUT SECURITY? Growing security concerns have also pushed Cairo towards a more active stance, analysts say. A [USN:L6N43V132 TEXT:"drone strike"] on two gas vessels at the Mediterranean port city of Damietta in July underscored that Egypt could not expect to keep itself fully isolated from the conflict. "I think they realise that they can't be on the sidelines about this indefinitely," said H. A. Hellyer, a scholar at the Royal United Services Institute think tank. For the authorities, the economic and security concerns were "one and the same," he said. Saudi Arabia and Egypt also have a shared interest in securing shipping through the Red Sea, an outlet for Saudi oil blocked from leaving the [USN:L1N4100GE TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"]. Egypt earns billions of dollars a year from fees on Suez Canal traffic. These overlapping concerns mean "Saudi Arabia's security constitutes a dimension of Egyptian national security," said Sherif Aref, an Egyptian political researcher and journalist. WHAT SORT OF MILITARY DOES EGYPT BRING TO THE TABLE? Egypt has one of the Arab world's largest armed forces, with hundreds of thousands of active personnel and large air, land and naval inventories, according to military analysts. Egypt sources equipment from a range of countries, and its air force operates US-made F-16s, French Rafales and Russian-made MiG-29s. Egypt receives about $1.3 billion a year in US military aid, which helps fund its purchases of American military equipment. Washington waived [USN:L6N45N0G9 TEXT:"human rights conditions"] on a tranche of the funds this year after what it called Cairo's "helpful role" since the Iran war began. In the years after the 2011 uprising that ousted President Hosni Mubarak, the armed forces fought a counterinsurgency campaign against Islamist militants in the Sinai Peninsula. Egypt also contributed air and naval forces to the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015, and conducted airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Libya during that country’s civil war. Egypt has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War, when its troops joined the US-led coalition to drive Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Nearly three decades earlier, President Gamal Abdel Nasser had sent Egyptian forces into Yemen in a costly intervention later compared to the US involvement in the Vietnam War. WHAT SORT OF SUPPORT IS LIKELY? Sisi's speech and subsequent statements have not specified what sort of military forces, if any, Egypt would ultimately intend to send. A deployment of Egyptian troops inside Yemen itself is unlikely, military analysts say. More likely interventions might include air defence and naval support, said Samir Ragheb, a retired Egyptian military officer who heads the Arab Foundation for Development and Strategic Studies think tank. "The threats, missiles and drones, require air defence and air forces," he said, adding that the navy could be used for protecting ships, naval operations against piracy and protecting the Saudi coastline. Still, the entry of another large conventional Arab military would not "suddenly solve the Houthi problem", said Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London. "The Houthis are difficult precisely because they generate disproportionate effect through missiles, drones, dispersed forces and geography. Egypt cannot bomb that problem away," he said. "What Cairo can do is strengthen Saudi resilience, improve Red Sea control, share the defensive burden and increase the political cost of continued attacks."

FAST

Oct 19 : AI-linked stocks bounced back on Monday from a bruising selloff last week as yields on government bonds dropped and crude oil prices eased, while CoreWeave gained following a rating upgrade. Its shares were up 2.4 per cent in choppy trading after losing a quarter of their value last week as the neocloud company's $50 billion debt triggered a crisis of confidence, sparking a global selloff across AI and tech stocks. "It's going to continue to be a factor, it's going to be a constant push-pull over time," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital. Goldman Sachs upgraded CoreWeave to "buy" from "neutral", saying tight computing capacity and the company's performance advantage over rival neocloud firms should lift annual recurring revenue per megawatt over the next two years. The brokerage said the recent pullback is a buying opportunity.

The yield on CoreWeave's bond maturing in 2031 fell 19.5 basis points to 15.13 per cent, easing from more than 16 per cent last week, according to Tradeweb data. Neocloud rival Nebius Group rose 3.4 per cent after tumbling more than 31 per cent in the past two weeks. Data center operators Applied Digital and IREN gained 8.5 per cent and 5 per cent, respectively. "You could certainly see a dead cat bounce today and maybe some continuation tomorrow, but it doesn't change the fact that the bond market is very skeptical about continuing to finance this without demanding higher and higher yields," added Hayes. The AI trade stumbled last week after a hot inflation reading raised bets for interest-rate hikes, fuelling concerns that heavily indebted AI companies could face higher borrowing costs. Morgan Stanley expects total AI investment to surge to $1.6 trillion in 2027 and $1.8 trillion in 2028. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped more than 11 per cent last week, with chip stocks among the hardest hit in the AI rout. The index has shed around $2 trillion in market value during an eight-session losing streak through Friday. It was last up 2.4 per cent, on course to snap its longest losing streak since October 2008. Intel climbed 4.5 per cent after J.P. Morgan upgraded the stock to "neutral" from "underweight", saying rising agentic AI workloads and tight supplies of advanced chips could support positive earnings estimate revisions through 2027. Nvidia added 1.5 per cent, AMD gained 3.6 per cent and Broadcom advanced 2.4 per cent, after all three sold off sharply last week. Memory-chip maker Micron Technology climbed 4.2 per cent after sliding nearly 15 per cent last week. Data-storage firms Sandisk, Western Digital and Seagate gained after steep declines last week. Earnings from megacap technology companies and hyperscalers could be the next test for the AI trade that powered Wall Street to record highs earlier this year, as investors look for evidence that earnings growth can offset concerns over valuations, debt and interest rates. Facebook-parent Meta Platforms and Elon Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX will report results later this week. Semiconductor companies Lam Research, Texas Instruments and Western Digital, are also set to report quarterly results. "The question this quarter is not whether AI will continue to grow, it's whether investors are still willing to pay a premium for that growth," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets.

Source: Reuters
